summary: Waluigi obtained fragments of testimony through channels he will not disclose describing a medical emergency that occurred shortly after the Brobot engagement at the ruined manor. According to these fragments, Luigi was brought to a medical facility near death after Mr. L's emergence and subdual. A surgeon identified only as 'Dr. Mario' civilian name possibly 'Dario' performed emergency surgery. Princess Daisy of Sarasaland was present. Pauline, Mayor of New Donk City, was present. Wario was present. Cranky Kong was present. None of these people should have been in the same room under normal circumstances. The testimony raises questions that Waluigi cannot answer but refuses to stop asking: Who is Dr. Mario? Why does Luigi call him 'Uncle Dario'? Why was Daisy behaving like family rather than a diplomatic ally? Why did Pauline call Luigi 'my man'? Why was Peach's name invoked as though she were alive? And why does every institutional actor in this account seem to already know what happened before being told? Waluigi has assembled what he can. The picture is incomplete. description:
Waluigi must begin with a warning that applies to this entire entry: NONE of this is confirmed through independent verification. The testimony reached Waluigi through a chain of sources that includes at least one Boo informant, a Regency clerk who was bribed with counterfeit currency possibly Wario's and a partial transcript that may or may not have been fabricated after the fact. Waluigi presents this account because the details are too specific to be pure invention, too consistent with known intelligence to be random fabrication, and too disturbing to ignore.

If even HALF of what follows is true, Waluigi's understanding of several key figures in this crisis requires fundamental revision.

## Context: What Preceded This Event


The Battle of the Brobot occurred on 3-4 Aethel, 1040 BF. Mr. L emerged during a ghost-clearing operation at the ruined manor. A Brobot appeared origin still unexplained. Multiple combatants were injured. Archie was blasted through a wall by a laser beam. Bones was grabbed and nearly killed. Mr. L was subdued through unknown means freezing mid-punch and going limp as though someone had flipped a switch.

Byscilla Danos executed what she called 'Phase One' of a containment protocol that the Mages' Guild had apparently prepared in advance. She reported: 'Target subdued. We have a target and got a signed spell scroll from Archie.'

What happened AFTER the subdual is what this testimony concerns. According to multiple fragments, Luigi not Mr. L, but LUIGI, restored to his own personality was in critical condition. The subdual itself may have caused severe neurological trauma. Whatever mechanism forced Mr. L back into dormancy did not do so gently.

Luigi was transported to a medical facility. The testimony describes what happened in the waiting room and the corridor outside the surgical theater.

## The Surgeon: 'Dr. Mario'


The most explosive element of the testimony is the identity of the surgeon who operated on Luigi.

According to the fragments, the doctor introduced himself or was referred to by staff as 'Dr. Mario.' Luigi, in moments of semi-consciousness before being prepped for surgery, called him 'Uncle Dario.' The doctor reportedly corrected this with visible emotion: 'That's Dr. Mario to you.' Then, softer: 'But I always loved when he called me that.'

Waluigi needs to address this directly because it threatens to collapse several load-bearing assumptions of the current investigation.

### Possibility One: 'Dr. Mario' Is Mario

This is the reading that makes Waluigi's head hurt the most.

Mario has been missing since approximately 1039 BF. Waluigi has documented the disappearance extensively the 985 BF Personnel Reallocation, the border town sighting in civilian clothes, the Star Fountain reunion where Luigi said 'Nothing can hurt us as long as we're together,' and then the SECOND separation that left Luigi operating alone under Mages' Guild contract.

If 'Dr. Mario' is Mario operating under the civilian name 'Dario,' it would mean Mario has been hiding in plain sight as a medical professional. The red cap gone. The overalls replaced by surgical scrubs. The hero of the Mushroom Kingdom performing surgery on his own brother while the world thinks he vanished.

This interpretation is supported by several details in the testimony. The emotional familiarity. The use of 'Uncle Dario' which could be a cover identity Luigi uses to maintain plausible deniability about their relationship. A brother cannot publicly be a brother if one of them is supposed to be missing. But an 'uncle' who is a doctor? That is a relationship that can exist on paper without triggering the warrant charges that include 'Conspiracy to Withhold Material Information regarding Mario's location.'

Luigi calling Mario his 'uncle' in public would be a LIE but a lie that protects them both. If anyone asks, Luigi has an uncle named Dario who is a doctor. Not a missing brother. Not the most wanted man in Mushroom Kingdom intelligence circles. Just an uncle. Just a doctor. Just a man who happens to look exactly like the plumber who disappeared.

The 'Uncle Dario' cover would also explain something that has always bothered Waluigi about Daisy's relationship with Luigi. Publicly, Daisy and Luigi have been presented as romantic partners appearing together at sporting events, kart races, party games. Waluigi has seen them side by side at DOZENS of events. The public narrative is boyfriend and girlfriend. But in this testimony, Daisy does not behave like a girlfriend. She behaves like FAMILY. She calls Luigi 'my baby nephew.' She screams with the particular fury of someone whose bloodline is being threatened, not someone whose romantic interest is in danger.

Waluigi's theory: If Mario is 'Dario,' and if Daisy is connected to the Mario family through a relationship that predates the public narrative, then the 'Luigi and Daisy are dating' story was always COVER. A convenient fiction that explained why the Princess of Sarasaland maintained close contact with one of the Mario Brothers without anyone asking uncomfortable questions about WHICH Mario Brother she was actually connected to, or WHY.

Daisy being Luigi's aunt through marriage to Mario under the name 'Dario,' or through some other family connection would mean her entire public persona as Luigi's girlfriend was a carefully maintained deception. Every kart race. Every tennis tournament. Every party game where they appeared as a couple. All of it was theater designed to provide a plausible public explanation for a family connection that could not be acknowledged without exposing Mario's location.

Waluigi finds this interpretation simultaneously outrageous and horrifyingly consistent with the available evidence.

### Possibility Two: 'Dr. Mario' Is a Separate Person

The less dramatic interpretation: 'Dario' is genuinely Mario's uncle or cousin. A relative who went into medicine rather than plumbing. A family member whose resemblance to Mario is genetic rather than identical. Luigi calling him 'Uncle Dario' is LITERAL, not cover.

This interpretation is simpler but creates its own problems. If the Mario family has a member who is a practicing surgeon, why has this person never appeared in ANY public record connected to the Mario Brothers? Why would a doctor share the surname and general appearance of the kingdom's most famous hero without anyone commenting on it? Why would this person be available for emergency surgery on a classified patient in a facility that may or may not be Ironmend Bastion?

Waluigi's assessment: the SIMPLER explanation requires MORE coincidences than the complicated one. A secret uncle-surgeon who appears at exactly the right moment is less plausible than Mario himself, operating under cover, maintaining proximity to his brother through a medical alias.

### Possibility Three: Waluigi Is Being Fed Disinformation

Waluigi must acknowledge this possibility. The testimony may be fabricated specifically to make Waluigi believe Mario has been found. Someone who knows Waluigi is investigating Mario's disappearance might plant exactly this kind of account emotionally compelling, detail-rich, impossible to verify to redirect Waluigi's investigation toward a false lead.

If 'Dr. Mario' is neither Mario nor a real relative but a fictional figure inserted into a fabricated transcript, then someone is manipulating Waluigi. The question becomes: who benefits from Waluigi believing Mario is alive and practicing medicine under an alias?

Waluigi cannot determine this. Waluigi notes the possibility and continues.

## The Waiting Room: What the Testimony Describes


The bulk of the testimony describes the waiting room during Luigi's surgery. The emotional temperature was volcanic. The cast of characters was improbable. The conversations were revealing in ways that the participants almost certainly did not intend.

### Daisy's Behavior

Daisy arrived at the facility and immediately demanded access to Luigi. She was denied only 'immediate family and her royal majesty, Princess Peach herself' were permitted inside. Daisy's response was fury on a scale that Waluigi has never associated with diplomatic protocol.

She called Luigi 'my baby nephew.' She said: 'While that boy was still in his first game, he begged me to make sure he stayed happy and healthy. And I promised him!'

Waluigi needs to address the phrase 'his first game.' In Mushroom Kingdom vernacular, 'game' can mean several things: a competitive event, a mission, a campaign. But the way Daisy used it 'his FIRST game' carries the weight of ORIGIN. The beginning. The moment when Luigi entered public life and needed someone to protect him.

If Daisy is family and this testimony strongly suggests she is then her promise to keep Luigi 'happy and healthy' predates the public career. She has been watching over him since the BEGINNING. Every kart race she appeared at alongside him was not a date. It was supervision. Every party game was not romance. It was an aunt keeping her promise.

This reframes Daisy's entire documented history. Her competence at the Second Summit. Her management of Sarasaland. Her quiet fury when systems fail. She has been operating with a PERSONAL stake in the Mario Brothers' survival that she has hidden behind a fake romantic narrative for what appears to be DECADES.

Waluigi's respect for Daisy was already considerable. It has now increased to levels that Waluigi finds structurally uncomfortable.

### The 'Princess Peach'

Invocation

The testimony mentions that access to Luigi was restricted to immediate family and 'her royal majesty, Princess Peach herself.' Peach has been dead since 955 BF. Her name should not appear in active access protocols at a medical facility in 1040 BF.

Waluigi has three interpretations:

One: The protocol is OLD. Written decades ago and never updated. Peach's name remains on a list that nobody has bothered to revise because bureaucracy outlives the people it was designed to serve. This is the boring interpretation and therefore probably correct.

Two: The protocol is ACTIVE. Someone with authority has maintained Peach's name on access lists deliberately either as a dead key that no one should be able to use, or as a living authorization for someone using Peach's identity. If a secret heir exists if Peach's child with Thornpaw survived that child might operate under the mother's access privileges. This interpretation makes Waluigi dizzy.

Three: The person who stated the protocol was using 'Princess Peach' as a CODE. A signal to other initiated parties that the situation was of the highest classification. Invoking a dead princess's name as an access credential is exactly the kind of theatrical security measure that the Regency and the Mages' Guild would consider clever.

Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct.

### The Question of Mario's Location

During the waiting room chaos, 'Dr. Mario' was asked about Mario the public Mario, the missing hero. The response, as recorded in the testimony: 'Mario can't come right now. He's far away on the front lines, risking it all for us against Bowser's legions.'

Daisy's response: 'For what? You going to tell me Peach has been kidnapped again, too?'

The staff member's response: 'That's classified information.'

Daisy: 'I was FUCKING joking. Are you kidding me?'

Waluigi needs to parse this carefully.

If 'Dr. Mario' IS Mario, then his staff providing a cover story about 'Mario being on the front lines' is part of the deception. Mario cannot be present as a surgeon AND absent on the front lines unless two separate narratives are being maintained simultaneously one for the public, one for those inside the facility.

The 'Peach kidnapped' exchange is more troubling. Daisy made a SARCASTIC comment. The staff member's response 'That's classified information' implies that someone, somewhere, is running an operation under the heading of 'Peach kidnapped.' In 1040 BF. Eighty-five years after Peach's assassination.

Either someone is using Peach's name as a mission codename 'Operation Peach Kidnapped' or similar or there is classified information about Peach's status that contradicts the official death record. Waluigi does not have enough evidence to determine which. Waluigi's headache has intensified.

### Pauline's Presence

Mayor Pauline of New Donk City arrived and referred to Luigi as 'my man.' Her behavior was that of a romantic partner in crisis desperate, emotional, focused entirely on Luigi's survival.

If Daisy is Luigi's aunt rather than his girlfriend, then Pauline being Luigi's ACTUAL romantic partner resolves the relationship question cleanly. The public 'Luigi and Daisy' narrative served as cover. The private reality is 'Luigi and Pauline.'

This makes a certain amount of sense. Pauline's position as mayor of New Donk City places her outside the Mushroom Kingdom's direct political sphere. A relationship between Luigi and Pauline would attract less factional attention than one between Luigi and a foreign princess. If the goal was to protect Luigi's personal life from becoming political leverage which, given the warrant situation, was a reasonable concern then publicizing a fake relationship with Daisy while maintaining a real one with Pauline is exactly the kind of misdirection that someone with intelligence training would arrange.

Who arranged it? Waluigi does not know. But the sophistication of the cover maintained across decades of public appearances, sporting events, and social functions suggests institutional support rather than personal initiative. Luigi is not cunning enough to maintain a deception this complex on his own. Someone HELPED him. The Mages' Guild. The Regency. Daisy herself. Mario. Possibly all of the above.

### Wario's Appearance

Wario appeared in the waiting room and immediately began antagonizing everyone. This is completely consistent with Wario's documented behavior and requires no special analysis.

However, several details from Wario's interactions are significant:

Wario claimed he needed to 'clear up a few things' with Mario and that 'my people had some very concerning intelligence to share.' This implies Wario has intelligence networks that have generated actionable information about Mario. Given Wario's financial operations and underworld contacts, this is plausible. Wario may know things about Mario's situation that even Waluigi does not.

Wario mentioned his cancer going into remission 'not long after the faking of my death and Warioland's first dissolution.' Waluigi's assessment: the cancer was REAL but its severity was exaggerated to make the faked death more convincing. The remission is genuine. The 'terminal' diagnosis was fabricated to provide motive for a plausible suicide. This is exactly the kind of layered deception Wario excels at embedding real medical information inside a larger fraud to make the whole package more convincing.

Wario also offered to 'speak to Dr. Mario instead' about his cancer remission, treating the surgeon as though he were an ordinary doctor. Either Wario does not know that 'Dr. Mario' might be Mario, or Wario DOES know and is performing ignorance. With Wario, both are equally plausible.

Waluigi would like the record to note that Wario's appearance at the facility constitutes a PUBLIC INDECENCY CHARGE by proxy because Waluigi was mentioned by name in connection with an incident that Waluigi has ALREADY BEEN PUNISHED FOR and does not wish to discuss further. Daisy's comment about Waluigi's 'public appearance being strictly regulated' is accurate and Waluigi resents that it was stated in front of Wario, who will absolutely use it as leverage later.

### Cranky Kong's Appearance

Cranky Kong appeared at the facility 'off his meds' and immediately began using language that Waluigi will not reproduce. He claimed responsibility for Luigi's injuries 'I blew him away earlier with my Coconut Gun for crossing me' which contradicts the established account of Mr. L's emergence being the cause.

Waluigi's assessment: Cranky was lying or delusional. His claim is inconsistent with every other account of the Brobot incident. However, Cranky's mention of DK hiding his original Coconut Gun is potentially significant for reasons unrelated to this particular incident it suggests internal Kong family conflicts that parallel the Mario Brothers' fractured relationships.

Cranky was eventually redirected when Pauline received urgent intelligence requiring her to leave for Kong Island airport. The nature of that intelligence is unknown but prompted immediate departure, suggesting a crisis of considerable magnitude.

### The Pharmaceutical

Incident

The testimony's final fragment describes Wario encountering Cranky Kong in the facility's corridors and proposing a joint robbery of the hospital pharmacy. An unidentified individual possibly a janitor, possibly an orderly, possibly someone with no medical credentials whatsoever offered to forge prescriptions in exchange for Cranky's participation.

The individual also mentioned having 'a pretty cool idea for the lawsuit that would follow' if Cranky 'accidentally died from the phony prescriptions overdose.'

Waluigi notes this exchange because it demonstrates the complete breakdown of institutional security at the facility. If Wario and Cranky Kong can openly discuss pharmacy robbery and prescription fraud in a corridor where a classified patient is undergoing emergency surgery, then the facility's security protocols are either deliberately lax or have been compromised.

This supports Waluigi's broader assessment that institutional competence in the Mushroom Kingdom has degraded to the point where NOTHING works as intended and EVERYONE is operating according to personal agendas rather than organizational mandates.

## The Surgery Itself


The testimony provides minimal information about the actual surgical procedure. 'Dr. Mario' stated that Luigi was 'on the verge of brain death' and that saving him was uncertain. He referenced an 'Extra Life' in Mushroom Kingdom medical terminology, this refers to emergency resuscitation protocols derived from Star Power applications. The phrase 'I won't let an Extra Life be wasted after what's happened today' suggests the facility had access to magical medical resources that are not available at standard hospitals.

The outcome of the surgery is not documented in the testimony fragments Waluigi has obtained. Luigi appeared alive and operational at Raventree Manor in subsequent events, so the surgery was presumably successful. But the gap between 'verge of brain death' and 'functional ghost hunter' is ENORMOUS, and whatever happened in that surgical theater may have changed Luigi in ways that are not yet apparent.

Waluigi wonders whether Luigi's subsequent behavior the Poltergust escape, the silence on the Mr. L question, the apparent willingness to work for the Guild might be partially explained by neurological changes resulting from emergency surgery performed by a man who may or may not be his brother operating under a false name.

## What This Changes


If the testimony is authentic and Waluigi rates it as PARTIALLY AUTHENTIC based on internal consistency and correlation with known intelligence then several elements of the current crisis require reinterpretation.

Mario's disappearance may not be a disappearance at all. It may be an identity change, with Mario operating as 'Dr. Dario' in a medical capacity, maintaining proximity to Luigi while remaining invisible to the factions hunting him. The 985 BF Personnel Reallocation may have been the Regency's attempt to neutralize him, and Mario responded not by fleeing east but by becoming someone else entirely.

Luigi and Daisy's relationship may have been fabricated to provide cover for a genuine family connection Daisy as aunt, not girlfriend which in turn may connect to Mario's hidden identity as 'Dario.' If Daisy married into the Mario family under a name that the public does not associate with the Mario Brothers, her entire diplomatic career gains an additional layer of motive.

Luigi and Pauline's relationship may be the ACTUAL romantic connection, hidden behind the Daisy cover for political protection. Pauline's emotional response in the testimony is consistent with a real partner, not a diplomatic contact.

The Mages' Guild's 'Phase One' may have included arranging Luigi's transport to a specific facility where 'Dr. Mario' was stationed. If the Guild knows Mario's cover identity, their leverage over Luigi becomes even more terrifying they do not merely know where Mario is, they have him working within their operational infrastructure as a medical asset.

Wario's intelligence networks may have independently identified 'Dr. Mario' as Mario, which would explain why Wario showed up at the facility and why he wanted to 'clear up a few things.' Wario does not visit hospitals out of concern for others. Wario visits because there is something he wants.

## Waluigi's


Assessment

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing the Mario disappearance. Waluigi has documented the Star Fountain reunion, the Eastern Passage theories, the 985 BF emergency session, the border town sighting. Waluigi has built a narrative of a hero who was exiled, who investigated a conspiracy alone, who reunited with his brother briefly before being separated again.

This testimony suggests a DIFFERENT narrative. One where Mario never fully left. One where the 'disappearance' was an identity death, not a physical one. One where Mario became someone else someone useful, someone invisible, someone who could remain near the people he loved without triggering the institutional responses that would follow if 'Mario' were found.

A plumber becomes a doctor. A hero becomes an uncle. A public figure becomes a private man with a new name and surgical scrubs instead of overalls.

Waluigi does not know if this is true. The testimony could be fabrication. The details could be misinterpreted. 'Uncle Dario' could be a genuine relative and the entire Mario-as-surgeon theory could be Waluigi seeing patterns in coincidence.

But Waluigi remembers something from the Mario entry: 'You don't abandon your identity unless you're trying to become someone else. Or unless someone MADE you abandon it.'

Mario without his cap. Mario in civilian clothes. Mario asking about routes east. And now, possibly, Mario in a surgical theater, saving his brother's life under a name that no one would think to search for.

If Mario chose to become 'Dr. Dario' if he chose anonymity, service, and proximity over heroism, fame, and visibility then Waluigi has been wrong about Mario in a way that Waluigi finds genuinely difficult to process.

Mario did not run. Mario did not hide. Mario became someone who could HELP without being SEEN.

That is either the most noble thing Waluigi has ever documented or the most elaborate cover story anyone has ever constructed.

Waluigi suspects it is both.

And somewhere in a hospital that no one will confirm exists, a surgeon who may or may not be the most famous plumber in history is washing his hands and checking on his brother's recovery and hoping that no one notices the resemblance.

Waluigi noticed.

Waluigi always notices.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi must be honest about the limitations of this entry. Unlike events Waluigi witnessed personally or documented through multiple independent sources, the ruined manor convergence comes primarily from participants whose accounts Waluigi cannot fully verify. Archie Miser provided the most detailed testimony, but Archie is a man who once convinced a tribunal he acted in 'justifiable magical defense' after killing someone in a public market. His version of events may be accurate. His version of events may also be carefully constructed to present himself in the best possible light. Waluigi has attempted to cross-reference where possible, but the chaotic nature of this event means that even honest witnesses might remember things differently than they occurred.

## What Waluigi Has Been Able to Confirm


Certain elements of this account are independently verified. The ruined manor exists—Waluigi has confirmed its location near the Thornwood through cartographic records. A teleportation circle was discovered there—multiple sources reference it, and Waluigi has obtained partial sketches of the geometric patterns. A warrant for Luigi's arrest was issued by Magistrate Toadsworth IV—Waluigi has seen copies of this document, and its authenticity appears genuine. An alliance calling itself the Cells of the Third Eye now operates in the region—Iron Legion intelligence confirms their existence, even if they dispute the organization's legitimacy.

These facts form the skeleton of the account.

Everything else is flesh that Waluigi has assembled from testimony, rumor, and educated guessing.

## The Circle and the Spirit — What Luigi Found


According to multiple sources, Agent L kicked aside a rug in the manor's central room and discovered the remnants of a teleportation circle etched in chalk and charcoal. The circle had been deliberately damaged—sections scratched out, connections severed—suggesting someone wanted to ensure it could never be used again. Or perhaps someone wanted it to APPEAR unusable while preserving its function for those who knew how to restore it. Waluigi cannot determine which interpretation is correct from available evidence.

More concerning is the spirit testimony that Luigi allegedly obtained before arriving at the manor. Waluigi has seen fragments of Luigi's notes—or documents claiming to be Luigi's notes—describing a communion with someone named Ashford. The spirit spoke of coordinates in the Thornwood, of documents 'sealed in iron' beneath a hanging tree, of coronations that were 'theater' while 'real power signed in blood not ink.' The spirit allegedly said the Crown's true heir 'walks among the Thornwood dead' and that the bloodline was 'broken at third branch.' If this testimony is authentic, it suggests the entire succession crisis is built on fundamental lies.

If it is fabricated, someone went to considerable effort to create compelling disinformation.

Waluigi notes that Luigi's final recorded words from the spirit were 'trust no crowns.' Sound advice, perhaps, but also convenient phrasing for anyone wanting to undermine legitimate authority. Waluigi is uncertain whether to treat this testimony as revelation or propaganda.

## The Ghost Swarm — Numbers Vary Considerably


Everyone agrees that ghosts appeared in the lord's chamber. The number varies dramatically depending on the source. Archie's account mentions 'over forty,' which would represent an unprecedented concentration of spectral activity. Bones—who fled first and therefore saw the initial manifestation—estimates 'more than twenty, maybe thirty.' A Regency operative who arrived later heard it was 'a dozen or so' from secondary sources. Waluigi suspects the actual number was somewhere in the middle range, with witnesses inflating or deflating based on how brave or practical they wished to appear.

What matters more than the exact count is that everyone fled. Agent L reportedly said 'it's time' when the ghosts appeared, suggesting he intended to fight. Archie reportedly said 'we can take them,' demonstrating his characteristic overconfidence. But within minutes, Bones had jumped from a balcony, Archie was retreating toward the master bedroom, and Luigi was left alone with whatever number of ghosts actually manifested. Luigi's reported response to being abandoned—'I'm used to it'—has been confirmed by multiple sources and carries emotional weight that suggests authenticity. People do not typically fabricate phrases that make them sound pathetic.

## Archie's Hospital Account —


The Most Questionable Section

This is where Waluigi's confidence in the narrative drops significantly. According to Archie, he fell approximately forty feet from a manor window, survived, woke up in Ironmend Bastion—the Iron Legion's premier medical facility—and discovered that everyone in his room had been murdered while he slept. The Mole was standing there smiling, offering him ritual components 'free of charge.' Archie refused, looted the corpses for supplies, disguised himself as a guard, and escaped the facility without being detected.

Waluigi has problems with this account. First, forty-foot falls are typically fatal or at minimum severely injurious. Archie claims he 'got lucky,' but luck of that magnitude strains credulity. Second, Ironmend Bastion is a heavily guarded facility—the idea that one man could disguise himself and walk out unchallenged suggests either exceptional skill or significant exaggeration. Third, the Mole killing an entire room of patients to offer Archie components is theatrical in a way that feels PERFORMED. Either the Mole operates according to a logic so alien that Waluigi cannot comprehend it, or Archie is embellishing what actually occurred.

Waluigi has attempted to verify the hospital massacre independently. Iron Legion sources confirm 'an incident' at Ironmend Bastion around the relevant timeframe, but details are classified. This could mean Archie's account is accurate and the Legion is covering up their security failure. It could also mean something different happened entirely and Archie constructed his narrative around a kernel of truth.

## The Warrant — This Document Waluigi Has Verified


Unlike the hospital account, the warrant for Luigi's arrest is documented and authentic. Waluigi has examined copies. The charges are real: Conspiracy to Withhold Material Information regarding Mario's location, Unauthorized Association with the Mages' Guild, Residual Mr. L Activities, and Obstruction of Ongoing Investigations. The probable cause section references 'one very talkative Boo informant'—which may be Waluigi's own source, suggesting that information Waluigi gathered has been used to build a case against Luigi. This is uncomfortable but not unexpected. Information flows in multiple directions.

What troubles Waluigi most is the authorization. The warrant was issued by Magistrate Toadsworth IV, who according to multiple sources 'usually doesn't do warrants' and 'is quiet unless it involves Peach.' Why would Toadsworth personally authorize this document? Why would Captain Toadette's name appear initially and then be crossed out for 'administrative error'? The Regency explanation is unsatisfying. Administrative errors do not typically result in Loyalist commanders being listed as authorizing officials on Regency warrants.

## The


Interrogation — Archie as Judge

According to witnesses from multiple factions, Archie appointed himself magistrate in the middle of an active battlefield and proceeded to evaluate each charge against Luigi. Luigi's responses to the charges, as reported by witnesses, are revealing. On Mario's location, he allegedly said: 'He's fine. Better than fine. He's doing what heroes do when no one else can. I can't say more.' This is consistent with the Eastern Passage documentation Waluigi has compiled—Luigi knows something about Mario's situation and considers it necessary rather than concerning. On the Guild association, Luigi allegedly said: 'They pay well, okay? And after everything, I needed something to do.' The loneliness in that response matches what Waluigi has observed of Luigi's current state.

On the Mr. L charges, Luigi reportedly became agitated, claiming he 'wasn't himself' and that 'someone else was driving while I was screaming in the back seat.' When Archie allegedly asked if Luigi did something evil during that period, Luigi went silent. Multiple witnesses confirm the silence. Whatever happened during the Mr. L incident, Luigi cannot or will not deny it directly. Before Archie could render any verdict, Luigi slammed his Poltergust into the ground and fled. Multiple witnesses confirm this. Luigi chose escape over judgment.

## The Alliance — Cells of the Third Eye


The most improbable element of this entire account is that three hostile factions agreed to work together afterward. Iron Legion operatives who had just decapitated Regency Toads agreed to serve alongside surviving Regency representatives. Archie—a known quantity to the Legion, a stranger to the Regency—became nominal leader. The organization named itself the Cells of the Third Eye, suggesting aspirations toward hidden knowledge and surveillance.

The roster, as Waluigi has reconstructed it, includes a troubling concentration of Iron Legion personnel. Byscilla Danos, Aemenor Evenflight, Hargram Fidger, Darno Spriggon, Warol Creeton, Rhak the Lost, Thornbury, and Manderaz the Mad—all Legion affiliated. Against this, the Regency contributed only three representatives: Gregir Fendelsohn, Terenzio Cassalanter, and Nine-Fingers Keene. The Liberated Toads added Lucky T, Bones, and Archie himself. The balance of power within this 'alliance' is heavily skewed toward Legion interests. This cannot be coincidental.

## Waluigi's


Theories and Extended Analysis

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing this event, and Waluigi has developed multiple theories about what actually occurred and what it means for the broader crisis. Waluigi presents these theories not as conclusions but as frameworks for understanding—each has supporting evidence and each has significant problems.

**Theory One: The Legion Orchestrated Everything**

The Iron Legion's presence at the manor was not coincidental. They arrived to 'protect' Archie at precisely the moment the Regency arrived to arrest Luigi. They had operatives in position. They knew where Archie was despite his escape from their own hospital. They brought enough personnel to dominate any resulting alliance. This suggests foreknowledge, planning, and strategic positioning that transforms the 'convergence' from chaotic accident to deliberate operation.

If the Legion orchestrated this event, their goals become clearer. They wanted Archie—a powerful fire mage with connections to the Raventree crisis—under their influence. They wanted Luigi discredited or driven underground, removing a potential ally from other factions. They wanted a cross-factional organization they could control from within while appearing to cooperate with enemies. The Cells of the Third Eye, under this theory, is a Legion front operation with Archie as an unwitting figurehead.

Supporting evidence: The Legion's dominant numbers in the alliance roster. Darno Spriggon's refusal to take orders from Archie—suggesting he answers to someone else. Byscilla's mysterious papers that influenced her decisions—possibly Legion intelligence briefings. The convenient timing of Legion arrival. Archie's presence in a Legion hospital before the convergence.

Problems with this theory: The Legion also suffered casualties during the fight. Thornbury took an arrow to the knee. If this was a planned operation, why allow their own people to be injured? Additionally, Archie's escape from Ironmend Bastion suggests the Legion did NOT have full control over his movements—unless the escape itself was permitted to establish Archie's sense of independence before drawing him back in.

Waluigi rates this theory as PLAUSIBLE but not confirmed.

**Theory Two: The Mole Is Running Everyone**

The Mole appears at critical moments throughout this crisis. The Mole appeared at the hospital offering Archie exactly what he needed. The Mole killed witnesses—the hospital patients—who might have complicated the narrative. The Mole operates according to patterns that no faction fully understands. What if the Mole is not serving any existing faction but rather manipulating ALL factions toward some independent goal?

Under this theory, the ruined manor convergence was engineered by the Mole to create chaos from which a new organization would emerge. The Mole ensured Archie survived the fall—perhaps through intervention Archie did not perceive. The Mole ensured Archie would return to the manor at the precise moment when factions were colliding. The Mole's offer of 'free' components was not generosity but investment—Archie's refusal does not matter if the Mole achieves their goals through other means.

Supporting evidence: The Mole's presence at the hospital is otherwise inexplicable. Why would the Mole be there? Why would the Mole kill those specific people? Why would the Mole offer help and accept refusal? These questions only make sense if the Mole's actual goal was accomplished regardless of Archie's response—perhaps simply ensuring Archie left the hospital and returned to the manor.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi has no evidence of the Mole's broader goals. This theory explains the Mole's behavior by assuming hidden purposes, which is circular reasoning. The Mole might simply be chaotic, opportunistic, or operating according to logic that appears purposeful but is actually random.

Waluigi rates this theory as POSSIBLE but highly speculative.

**Theory Three: Ashford's Testimony Is the Key**

What if the ruined manor convergence matters primarily because of what Luigi discovered, not because of the factional chaos that followed? Ashford's spirit provided coordinates, allegations about false coronations, claims that the true heir 'walks among the Thornwood dead.' If this testimony is accurate, someone powerful has reason to suppress it. The warrant for Luigi's arrest, the convergence of factions, the formation of a new alliance—all of this might be maneuvering around the REAL issue: what Ashford knew and who wants that knowledge controlled.

Under this theory, Toadsworth IV issued the warrant because he knows Ashford's testimony threatens the current power structure. The Regency wants Luigi arrested not for the stated charges but to interrogate him about what the spirit revealed. The Legion wants Archie controlled because Archie now travels with people who have access to that testimony. Everyone is reacting to Ashford, not to each other.

Supporting evidence: Toadsworth IV 'usually doesn't do warrants' but personally authorized this one. The warrant references the Star Fountain investigation and 'obstruction'—but what is being obstructed? The phrasing 'trust no crowns' directly challenges Regency legitimacy. If Ashford's claims about broken bloodlines and theatrical coronations are true, the entire Regency power structure is fraudulent.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi cannot verify that anyone besides Luigi actually knows what Ashford said. If the testimony is so dangerous, why hasn't Luigi been assassinated rather than warranted? A warrant creates legal process, witnesses, documentation. Assassination is cleaner. Unless someone wants Luigi alive for questioning—which supports this theory—or unless the warrant is cover for something else entirely.

Waluigi rates this theory as COMPELLING but requiring more evidence.

**Theory Four: Luigi Engineered His Own Escape**

This theory troubles Waluigi because it casts Luigi in a more calculating light than Waluigi has previously considered. What if Luigi WANTED to be confronted at the manor? What if the Poltergust escape was planned, not panicked? What if Luigi used the chaos to disappear while leaving others to deal with the consequences?

Consider: Luigi knew a warrant existed or would exist. He knew the Regency was looking for him. He knew the Iron Legion had interest in Archie. By positioning himself at the manor during a ghost crisis, he created conditions where multiple factions would collide. His 'escape' during the interrogation removed him from immediate custody while leaving Archie to form an alliance that would occupy both the Legion and the Regency. Luigi gets freedom to pursue whatever he's actually doing—possibly following Ashford's coordinates to the Thornwood—while his pursuers are distracted by a new organization that he is no longer part of.

Supporting evidence: Luigi's Poltergust is not typically an escape tool—it is designed for ghost capture. Using it to scatter everyone and flee suggests preparation, not panic. Luigi's phrase 'I'm used to it' when abandoned could be resignation OR could be performance—the appearance of the abandoned brother who is actually manipulating events. Luigi has survived things that should have killed him. He is not as helpless as he appears.

Problems with this theory: Waluigi has documented Luigi's emotional struggles extensively. The man Waluigi has observed seems genuinely lost, not cunningly strategic. This theory requires Luigi to be acting, which contradicts everything Waluigi thinks he knows about Luigi's character. Unless Waluigi has been fooled. Unless everyone has been fooled. Unless Luigi's apparent vulnerability is the most sophisticated deception of all.

Waluigi rates this theory as UNLIKELY but not impossible. Waluigi does not WANT this theory to be true because it would mean Waluigi has fundamentally misread Luigi's character.

**Theory Five: Coincidence and Chaos**

The simplest explanation: nothing was orchestrated. The Legion arrived because they were tracking Archie after his hospital escape. The Regency arrived because they had a warrant and intelligence about Luigi's location. The ghosts appeared because the manor is haunted and intruders triggered defensive manifestations. The alliance formed because desperate people in dangerous situations sometimes cooperate despite historical enmity. There is no grand plan. There is no hidden orchestrator. There is only chaos producing outcomes that APPEAR purposeful in retrospect.

Waluigi resists this theory because Waluigi has spent months documenting conspiracies, patterns, and hidden connections. If the ruined manor convergence is simply chaos, it suggests that other events Waluigi has analyzed might also be chaos. The assassination conspiracy, the Eastern Passage, the Star Fountain reunion—all of these might be random events that Waluigi has forced into narrative frameworks because Waluigi needs to believe that meaning exists.

This possibility frightens Waluigi more than any conspiracy theory. A world of deliberate evil can be fought. A world of random chaos can only be survived.

Waluigi rates this theory as TERRIFYING and refuses to think about it further.

**What Waluigi Actually Believes**

After extensive analysis, Waluigi's working hypothesis is a combination of theories. Waluigi believes the Iron Legion saw an opportunity and exploited it—they did not create the convergence, but they positioned themselves to benefit from it. Waluigi believes Ashford's testimony is significant and that multiple parties are maneuvering to control or suppress that information. Waluigi believes the Mole has purposes that no one understands, and that the hospital incident served those purposes in ways that are not yet apparent. Waluigi believes Luigi fled because he had no better options, not because he engineered the situation—but Waluigi acknowledges uncertainty about Luigi's true capabilities.

Waluigi believes the Cells of the Third Eye will collapse, probably violently, when the Iron Legion's patience with the pretense of cooperation expires. The numbers favor them. The positioning favors them. Archie's nominal leadership is exactly that—nominal. When the Legion decides they have extracted sufficient value from this arrangement, they will dispose of non-Legion members and claim whatever Archie has accomplished.

Waluigi believes Archie knows this, or suspects it, and is racing to accomplish his goals—reaching his friends on other planes—before the betrayal comes. The teleportation circle in the manor, the components the Mole offered, Byscilla's claimed expertise in planar travel—all of these point toward Archie's actual priority. He does not care about factional politics. He cares about rescue. The alliance is a tool, and he will discard it when it stops being useful.

This makes Archie either admirably focused or dangerously amoral. Waluigi suspects both.

**On Manderaz the Mad**

Waluigi must note that Manderaz the Mad is Iron Legion despite the name suggesting otherwise. The 'Mad' appellation apparently refers to combat behavior rather than political affiliation—Manderaz fights with a ferocity that other Legion operatives find excessive even by their standards. Including Manderaz in the alliance roster adds another Legion-loyal fighter to an already Legion-dominated group. Whether Manderaz's 'madness' makes them unpredictable even to Legion command is unknown. They might be a loose cannon that complicates Legion control. They might be exactly as controlled as every other Legion operative, with the 'mad' reputation serving as cover for calculated brutality.

Waluigi has not been able to interview Manderaz directly. Sources describe them as 'difficult to approach' and 'prone to violence when questioned.' This is either genuine instability or very effective deterrence against investigation. Waluigi will attempt contact through intermediaries if opportunity presents.

**On the Thornwood Coordinates**

Ashford's spirit provided specific coordinates: 47°N 23°W from castle ruins, beneath a hanging tree where the Toad Council fell. Waluigi has attempted to identify this location. Multiple castle ruins exist in the region. Multiple hanging trees have historical significance. The Toad Council's fall is documented—a massacre during the early civil war period—but the location of that massacre is disputed by different sources.

If Waluigi can identify the correct location, Waluigi might be able to retrieve the 'documents sealed in iron' that Ashford referenced. These documents allegedly prove that the current heir is illegitimate and that the coronation was theater. Such documents would be explosive. They would validate Loyalist claims while undermining Regency authority. They might also reveal information that neither faction wants public—the 'real power signed in blood not ink' suggests agreements that transcend the official conflict.

Waluigi intends to investigate these coordinates personally. This is dangerous. The Thornwood has a reputation for consuming those who enter unprepared. But Waluigi has spent months documenting others' discoveries. Perhaps it is time for Waluigi to make discoveries of his own.

**On Luigi's Silence**

The moment that haunts Waluigi most from this account is Luigi's silence when asked if Mr. L 'did something evil.' Multiple witnesses confirm the silence. Luigi—who defended himself on every other charge, who explained his Guild association, who insisted he 'wasn't himself' during the Mr. L period—could not or would not deny doing evil.

What did Mr. L do? The Mr. L incident is poorly documented in available sources. Waluigi knows it involved dimensional manipulation, possibly mind control, possibly collaboration with forces hostile to the Mushroom Kingdom. But specifics are classified, redacted, or simply not recorded. Luigi's silence suggests the truth is worse than rumor. If he could deny evil, he would have denied it. His silence is confession by omission.

This complicates Waluigi's understanding of Luigi considerably. Waluigi has portrayed Luigi as a sympathetic figure—the abandoned brother, the lonely ghost hunter, the man trying to do right in impossible circumstances. But sympathetic figures do not go silent when asked about evil. Sympathetic figures deny, explain, contextualize. Luigi did none of these things.

Waluigi does not know what to do with this information. Waluigi does not know if it changes the overall assessment of Luigi's character or if it reveals a single dark chapter in an otherwise decent person's life. Waluigi knows only that the silence happened, that it was witnessed, and that it means something Waluigi has not yet understood.

**Final Thoughts on the Convergence**

The ruined manor convergence was either a turning point or a footnote. Either the Cells of the Third Eye will accomplish something significant—retrieving Archie's friends, uncovering Ashford's documents, changing the balance of power—or they will collapse into mutual destruction and be remembered only as another failed alliance in a war filled with failed alliances.

Waluigi will continue monitoring this situation. Waluigi will attempt to verify Archie's more questionable claims. Waluigi will investigate the Thornwood coordinates if possible. Waluigi will track Luigi's movements if Luigi can be tracked.

And Waluigi will remember that in the middle of chaos, when asked to judge a man he barely knew on charges he could not fully evaluate, Archie Miser attempted something like fairness. He asked for Luigi's side. He listened to the responses. He was reaching a verdict—we will never know what verdict—before Luigi fled.

In a world where factions kill each other over decades-old grievances, where conspiracies nest inside conspiracies, where the truth is always obscured by layers of deception and counter-deception, one pyromaniac trying to be fair in a haunted manor might be the most hopeful thing Waluigi has documented.

Or it might be another performance, another manipulation, another lie dressed in the clothing of justice.

Waluigi does not know. Waluigi rarely knows. Waluigi documents anyway.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi must break this down into its component failures, because the sheer density of incompetence and malice requires a masterclass in analysis.

## The Repossessed Heal (Parson Pellinost's Hustle)


Archie was resting. A man named Parson Pellinost—claiming to be a Mages' Guild doctor—breezed past the magical wards, produced a crumpled medical card, and healed Archie. 

'You are now in my debt,' Pellinost declared.

Archie, possessing the financial instincts of a man who already owes 2,062 gold pieces for a broken rope, demanded a 'refund.' 

Waluigi wants everyone to pause and appreciate the sheer, unadulterated PETTINESS of what happened next. Parson Pellinost did not argue. He did not file a grievance. He simply reached out and FORCEFULLY DRAINED THE HEALING MAGIC BACK OUT OF ARCHIE'S BODY. Archie immediately felt terrible again. Pellinost told him to 'use his card if he needed him' and walked away.

Waluigi hates the Mages' Guild. Waluigi despises their bureaucracy. But Waluigi respects a good grift. Healing someone, establishing a debt, and literally *repo'ing their health* when they complain is a level of aggressive capitalism that brings a tear to Waluigi's eye. Wario would be taking notes.

## The Manifestation of Agony


Following the medical extortion, Darno Spriggon (the man with the stolen Legion ring) offered to 'show Archie a monster.' Archie immediately saw a giant fireball monster that no one else could see. It chased him upstairs.

Let Waluigi translate this for the layperson: The Guild/Legion alliance deployed targeted, localized psychological warfare against Archie. They manifested his 'pure agony' into an illusion visible only to him, designed to isolate him from the group. It worked flawlessly because Archie's default response to psychological trauma is to run away and lock himself in a dark room.

## The Oracle's


Intervention and the 'Starlight' Fraud

Inside the locked room, the Oracle appeared, healed Archie (presumably without charging him interest), and dropped a massive piece of intelligence: The Mages' Guild plans to use Archie's research and his 'entropy-bleeding' magical signature to establish interdimensional travel on demand. Archie is not a prisoner; he is a BATTERY.

Before they could process this, Iron Legion guards breached the room to detain the Oracle. Archie tried to negotiate. During the standoff, they noticed Bones, asleep in a bed, having not woken up in hours.

The Legion guards claimed Bones was suffering from 'Starlight Fever'—a magical malady causing uncontrollable surges. The Oracle immediately called them liars, stating Starlight Fever doesn't affect Toads.

Archie then managed to steal/read a Legion tablet. Waluigi has reviewed the transcript of this tablet, and it is a masterpiece of bureaucratic evil:

**FALSIFIED DIAGNOSIS:** *Starlight Fever.* (Note: Zero arcane surge activity detected. Diagnosis does not match patient presentation.)
**ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS:** *Somnium Captivus — Induced Arcane Coma via Compound Sedation.* (Deliberate administration of a dual-layer mundane/arcane sedative. Unlawful detainment under Article 9.)

The Iron Legion wasn't treating Bones. They had chemically and magically lobotomized him to keep him quiet after he successfully infiltrated Aegis Command. They filed the real diagnosis right beneath the fake one on the same tablet, because the Iron Legion's obsession with accurate paperwork completely overrides their instinct for a cover-up.

Waluigi is offended. If you are going to drug a political prisoner and lie about it, KEEP TWO SEPARATE LEDGERS. Amateurs. WAH.

name: Warp Pipe Junction — The Shack, the Ladders, and the Five-Foot Crayfish
title: The Restricted City and the Opened Gate
date: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — Material clock; afternoon into the fight on the wall
status: Resolved — squad extracted; Junction not held
summary: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF. Toadette sits the pipe-edge after a rat does not come back. Embercap lies them through a Bowser Bros gate. The manor is a rust shack. They climb the ladders. Dewdrop goes down twice. Toadette becomes a five-foot crayfish. Embercap opens the winch. Big R carries the medic-scribe out. They do not get a guildmaster. They get a gate that works from the inside.

sections.name: The Edge of the Pipes
sections.overview:
Toadette stood at the lip of the Warp Pipe Junction and did not go down.

Behind her the army waited the way Loyalist armies wait: quiet, packed, watching the back of her head as if the next order might already be in her neck. In front of her the pipes breathed. Wet brick. Steam that smelled like old metal and someone else's destination. Condensation ran down the nearest mouth and made a black line in the mud.

She sat.

The thought she did not share with the ranks was small and ugly and correct. She should not have sent a rat to do reconnaissance. The rat had not come back. There was no body. There was no squeak. There was a hole in the afternoon the size of one animal and she put her weight on the brick instead of on the next order.

The army did not ask. That is what an army is for when it still trusts the back of a captain's head.

*WAH! Waluigi was not on that lip. Waluigi has the after-action and a captain who will not write the sentence 'I was wrong about the rat.' So Waluigi will write it. She sat there knowing. That is better than most officers Waluigi has audited, and it is still a missing rat.*

sections.name: Bowser Bros Only
sections.overview:
Halt.

The word came off the gate the way paint comes off a cheap sign: already peeling, still legally there. You may not enter. Restricted city. Bowser Bros only. The letters had been brushed on by someone who believed the name would do the rest of the work.

Embercap stepped forward with the crimson plume doing what it always does — making him visible on purpose.

“Can you make an exception,” he said, “to let us in.”

The gate did not move.

“We have a message for the guildmaster,” Embercap said. “We need to discuss matters.”

It was a lie. It was a clean lie. The kind of lie a field commander tells when the captain is still thinking about a rat and the army is still behind her and the only other option is to admit you have no paper.

They bought it.

A guard was assigned. The gates opened on a groan that had rust in it. A Goomba was given the four of them — Toadette, Embercap, Dewdrop, Big R, the Loyalist leadership in one stupid, hopeful line — and told to watch them.

“Alright,” Embercap said.

The Goomba said he would lead them to the manor.

The army stayed on the pipe side. That is the last honest fact about the front door.

sections.name: The Rust Shack
sections.imageCaption: The manor, as sold. Filed after the climb. The Goomba pointed here.
sections.overview:
Toadette could not tell if the Goomba was lying. That is not a metaphor. She looked at him and the read would not come. Poor town. Mud. A street that had given up on being a street.

“It's right in here,” the Goomba said, and pointed.

Rust. Old wood. A shack that had given up on being a building and become a warning that had not been written down. The roof sagged toward the alley. One window held a rag instead of glass. If a guildmaster slept here, the guild was already dead.

“Hmm,” Toadette said. “Thought it would be more of a forewarning.”

She waited.

Then: “Wait a minute.”

The pause was long enough to be rude.

“This isn't the guildmaster's house, is it.”

“What do you mean.”

“Well,” she said, and this is the sentence Waluigi wants carved on the Junction, “if the guildmaster is sleeping anywhere, he would be sleeping in a guildhouse, where he hosts his guild.”

“Well,” said the Goomba, “it's a poor town.”

“Hmm. Now that you mention it. This isn't the real house, is it, Goomba boy.”

The shack did not argue. Shacks never do. They wait for you to walk in anyway.

sections.name: You'll Have Real Fun
sections.overview:
A Koopa came up the way help comes up when it is not help.

“These boys giving you trouble.”

“Nah,” said the Goomba. “I was leading them to the house.”

“Ohhh. The house. You guys are going to have real fun.”

They got the sense it was a lie. Toadette said the next part out loud, because saying it out loud is how she keeps a squad from walking into a shack.

“We get the sense the grandmaster lives there.”

They walked away. The Goomba and the Koopa followed. The mud took their prints and kept them. Dewdrop stayed close enough to punch. Big R stayed close enough to be a wall.

“Leave us alone. We will report you to the authorities. We don't know the guild members personally.”

“You don't. That's the reason you went in the town.”

“Yeah… we're acquainted with him. Don't know their friends but umm. Uhh.”

They kept following.

“Don't worry,” one of them said. “We will take care of it for you.”

“Let's see some ID,” the Koopa asked, and the Goomba went to get the guards.

They ran.

The Koopa went, “Aw, sheet,” and charged Dewdrop. Dewdrop dodged and punched him. The sound was small and correct.

“Sorry for wasting your time,” someone said, already moving. “We will be off now.”

Behind them the gate they had talked through was already becoming a joke.

sections.name: The Ladders
sections.imageCaption: The wall after the lie. Five feet of crayfish. The army stayed at the pipes.
sections.overview:
The gate was closed.

They did not have much time. They decided the way Loyalists decide when the front door has become a joke: they climbed the castle ladders. Wood slick with pipe-steam. Rungs that remembered other hands. Other ladders already moving on the flanks.

Order: Embercap. Dewdrop. Toadette. Big R.

People ran down those other ladders to meet them. One of them threw a spear. The spear found Dewdrop on the rungs. She folded around it the way a body folds when the afternoon has already used her once. The climb did not stop. That is the sentence that should have ended the climb and did not.

Toadette waved her wand.

Her head shifted. Her body widened. She became a crab-like thing the after-action will try to dress and the honest measurement will call five feet — bigger than a tiny crab, not a monster from a mural, a giant crayfish by Junction standards. Wet armor. One claw that could hold a shell.

She charged a Koopa anyway. She grabbed it with the claw. The Koopa kicked. The claw did not discuss it.

*WAH! Five feet. Waluigi has been waiting his entire career for a Loyalist change of shape to be a dragon. He got a crayfish you could trip over. She still used it to hold a turtle. Competence does not require size. Waluigi resents how often it has size anyway.*

sections.name: Goomba on the Head
sections.overview:
Big R boosted Embercap.

“Here goes nothing,” Embercap said, and jumped for a Goomba's head.

The Goomba pulled a fast one and jumped on his.

Embercap stabilized with a Goomba standing on his skull like a bad idea that had found a perch. The plume bent. He leaned backward so the Goomba would hang off the back of his head — a gift, if it worked, for Dewdrop and Big R and maybe even the crayfish.

The Goomba tried the back.

“I'm not going to fall that easy,” the Goomba said.

Embercap decided to drop.

He fell. He hit the brick on his back. Big R smiled.

A mace swing. Another.

The Goomba was dead. First kill. The sound a Goomba makes when it stops being a guide is smaller than the speech it made about manors.

“You murderer,” a Koopa cried, which is a rich sentence from a gate that had promised real fun in a rust shack.

sections.name: Dewdrop Goes Down
sections.overview:
Dewdrop threw a torch. It was not powerful enough to start a fire worth the word. The flame licked wet brick and died like it had been insulted.

She used her staff. She helped Embercap up. A spear came. Embercap caught it. Wood on wood. His hands knew the work.

“Eat a turtle,” Embercap said to the Koopa, because the Junction had already decided what kind of poetry it wanted.

Dewdrop was hit. Dewdrop went unconscious. The staff clattered and stayed.

Toadette, still a crayfish, charged a bystander Koopa and knocked him back into his shell. She stayed glued to that one until he was down. She used what the new body had: poison spores, the kind of gift a five-foot crab should not have and did. The air went green and wrong.

Embercap ran to Big R, who had a Magikoopa now. Hat. Jump. The kind of enemy that refuses to be a place. Embercap climbed, taunted, went for the hat. The Magikoopa ducked and scolded him.

“What the hell are you doing.”

Embercap jumped for the head. Desperation, and he knew it.

The Magikoopa left the spot. Embercap grabbed the ladder, unharmed.

The Magikoopa left the spot again as Big R swung and missed.

Big R sighed. “This guy is too strong.”

sections.name: Dull Claws, Open Gate
sections.overview:
Big R charged the wall output and swung at a Koopa guard.

The bear — the tally's word, Big R's body — swung wildly and missed twice. Brick dust. A grunt that belonged to a siege that had been asked to do ladder work.

Embercap slid the ladder, threw a spear, missed.

Toadette swung again at the same Koopa, determined. She used a brick. It hurt the claw. One more like that and the claw would not be a claw. She missed.

Big R hit. A Koopa died. Another ran the roof. On that side there was a Koopa and a Magikoopa left.

The bear slashed from below. Toadette clawed a running Koopa.

She went closer.

“You're a coward, turtle boy.”

Koopas are not turtles. Someone said so. The archive is keeping both sentences because the wall did.

Embercap moved a ladder, climbed, found the winch that pulls the gates, and started hauling. Chain. Rust. The honest machine in a dishonest town.

The gates opened.

Big R took a spear and five gold off a Koopa corpse. He picked up Dewdrop's unconscious body and moved.

Embercap went downstairs and started throwing from cover.

“Keep doing what you're doing,” he said. “We're getting out of here.”

sections.name: Blessing on a Bear's Back
sections.overview:
Toadette clawed again and missed. The claws were dull from missing. That is not a joke. That is what happens when you spend a fight on one enemy and a brick.

Dewdrop woke up.

“Thanks for waking me back up.”

She used the quarterstaff and blessed her teammates from Big R's back. The words were short. The back was moving. For a breath the wall had a medic again.

Then she went unconscious again, because a Koopa swiped her, and the Magikoopa put a blast into the bear, and the bear fell. The blessing stayed. The body did not.

Embercap dragged Dewdrop toward the exit and pulled her through it.

Toadette hit the beaten-up Koopa who was still kicking. Big R finished him and used the shield to knock him away. He moved to the entrance and waited.

The crayfish came last.

The tally later tried to make the wall into a count. Waluigi is not printing that count here. The wall was long enough for a Koopa to keep hitting the bear, for a Magikoopa to leave twice and land once, and for a crayfish to stay on one shell until the brick taught it manners.

Toadette won the way Loyalists win when the plan is already a lie: the gate opened, the wounded left, and the captain did not leave first.

aftermath:
**Standing.** The Warp Pipe Junction is still a restricted mouth. The Loyalist four are on the army side of it again. They did not speak to a guildmaster. They spoke to a Goomba, a Koopa, a Magikoopa, and a winch.

**Personnel.** Dewdrop has been unconscious twice in one afternoon and is alive because Embercap dragged her and Big R carried her. Toadette's claws are dull. Embercap's lie is now a known method. Big R has a spear and five gold that used to belong to a corpse.

**Materiel.** One torch that would not start a fire. One spear caught in the air. One brick that hurt the wrong claw. The [[prop:prop_warp_pipe_restricted_notice|Bowser Bros restriction notice]] is still on the gate. The [[prop:prop_junction_ladder_tally|ladder tally]] is the only paper the wall produced, and Waluigi is not treating it as a sermon.

**Exposure.** The gate crew now has faces: a Loyalist captain who becomes a crayfish, a plume that lies, a scribe who will not stay down, and a bear who waits at the door.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The lie worked. The house did not.** Embercap sold a guildmaster and bought a shack. That is not a failure of nerve. That is what a restricted city does when you do not have paper. Waluigi will not scold the lie. Waluigi will scold anyone who walks into the shack after Toadette has already said the word guildhouse.

**2. Five feet is enough.** The crayfish was not a dragon. It held a Koopa, put spores in the air, and stayed on one enemy until the brick taught it manners. Scale is a Loyalist temptation. This fight did not need it.

**3. Dewdrop is the cost.** Speared on the climb, down, up, blessing, down. Extracted. If this squad keeps using ladders as a plan, file the next medic bill before the next lie.

**4. The rat is still missing.** She sat on the lip and knew. Waluigi is not printing a first hearing on what ate it.

**Recommendation.** Do not send vermin to map a pipe hub. Do not accept a manor that looks like a warning. If you must climb, open the winch first. Embercap already proved the gate has an inside.

name: Promo Mario
title: Promo Mario — A Sighting or a Sales Pitch?
date: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — provisional filing date, inferred after the 4 Aethel charred note; encounter undated

status: Amended — Revision 2 current (full account filed 5 Aethel, 1040 BF, evening); sequel filed the same night: Luigi found alive in the maintenance room, the corrupted Mario unmasked as an act, and a Director sighted with a remote — see The Cut and the Puppet Master
summary: Waluigi's morning filing reviewed an abridged newspaper clipping that ended with a successful portal home. The full account recovered the same evening contradicts that ending: the portal failed, Luigi vanished during a strange tape, a corrupted Mario stepped out of the television, and Wario's Apparition ran a song-laden game show before a Wario Inc. tablet's flashlight ended it. The newspaper was a teaser. Waluigi filed it, and is amending the record, loudly.
description:
Waluigi stopped at the name: [[prop:prop_promo_mario_newspaper_clipping|PROMO MARIO]]. The available newspaper account supplies no publisher, byline or issue date. It supplies churros, souvenir shirts and a very helpful corporation.

## What the paper says

Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores and Alistair of the Marshkeepers reportedly fell onto the set of the Nintendo Mania pilot. Their host introduced himself as Mario, taught them a video game and took them around Hollywood. Alistair collected souvenirs; Darian wanted proof of the journey, then a way home to his province.

The turn came with a Wario Inc. tablet. Darian displayed [Waluigi's account of the missing Mario](#/article/mario). The host read about Peach's assassination and the [Star Fountain reunion](#/article/star_fountain_reunion), dropped his phone and wept. Asked whether he was that Mario, he offered a name—not a remembered journey. His Luigi arrived with pizza; he said Peach was alive in the studio.

The report ends with Miyamoto arranging help and Dr. Takeda opening a sixty-second portal. Darian and Alistair stepped through with Nintendo charms. **Mario stayed behind.** The paper does not describe our missing hero coming home.

## What Waluigi can actually file

*WAH! I recognize the tablet passage. It is MY writing. A man crying after reading my article is not a second witness to the events in it. I would like Mario found, even if it means another unbearable celebration without me. This is not enough.*

Alistair also places Mario's disappearance in 955 BF. That is the year of [Peach's assassination](#/article/princess_peach); the archive places the fountain meeting in 1039 BF. A matching cap and brother do not settle that contradiction. The claimed souvenirs and photographs have not been authenticated here, and Peach never appears before the visitors in the account. Like the [charred note](#/article/charred_note_at_waluigis_door), this is another story to test, not permission to replace the old file.

reputationNotes._record: Deliberate abstention. This is a review of an abridged clipping, amended by a recovered account Waluigi did not witness; the encounter itself is undated and unverified, and the record's own status is unverified. No faction can be said to have changed its opinion of anyone on this evidence. Left empty on purpose — do not fill it without a confirming filing.

waluigiAssessment:
**The mistake, filed honestly.** This is the assessment I should have written this morning, and I could not write it then because I did not know the morning was incomplete. I filed a reading of a reading. The newspaper was itself abridged — it ended at the first happy beat — and I treated a headline as a source. That is the whole failure, and I will not dilute it by blaming the paper alone.

1. **I never asked for the rest of the article.** A clipping with a clean ending is a bid, not a report. The full account shows the paper cut the portal failure, the tape, the missing brother, the corrupted Mario and an entire Wario song cycle. One question — *what happened after the farewell?* — was the whole file.
2. **The date error was a clue, not the error.** I filed 955 BF as a flaw in an unverified clipping. The full account treats 955 BF as the disappearance year, and it does so insistently. That is a claim, not a typo. Somebody in that world has been told the assassination and the disappearance were the same event — which is exactly what the charred note wants the archive to believe, and exactly what the archive does not believe about the 1039 BF fountain.
3. **The ending was the tell.** A corporate rescue with a sixty-second portal, crying staff and a generous goodbye is a good ending. It is so good that I stopped checking whether the machine worked. The portal did not open. I filed the goodbye and left the machine out of the record.
4. **What the fuller account does not fix.** Darian and Alistair remain one source. The studio Mario is still not proven to be our Mario. The Doughnut World reading is Darian's theory, not a documented plane. The figure that came out of the television is not filed as a Mario at all — it is filed as something that wears the name.
5. **What I actually learned.** I am not the only person who can be misled by my own archive. A man in another layer of the world read my article and cried at it. I will spend some time deciding whether that makes my article good.

**Recommendation:** find Luigi; obtain the original tape and the security footage; interview Darian and Alistair separately; and do not go to the exit, because every exit in that building is a trap.

## Part One: Two People Fall Out of the Sky

Mario was reading a book when the lights above the sound stage flickered twice, and two figures dropped out of nowhere, hit the floor of the **Nintendo Mania** pilot set, and lay still long enough for a stagehand to scream.

He looked up. He closed the book. He crossed the floor with the careful cheer of a man who has decided the alternative is a lawsuit.

"Oh! Uh—Hey paisanos! I'm Mario!" He spread his arms wide. "But you probably knew that already."

The taller of the two strangers — fine dark clothes, a noble's collar, dust still settling in his hair — was staring at the cameras. The shorter one, a steward, had his hand on a weapon that did not exist in this building.

Mario studied the pair. Then he glanced at the camera, squared his shoulders, and did what he always did when the lights were hot and the answer was missing. He performed.

"Now, you may be wondering—" he said, and stopped. "Two people fall in from the sky, unknown to him. Sorry, who are these guys again?" He turned to the camera, waited, nodded as though the answer had arrived. "Oh, right. So anyways—you and your friend here arrived at a very *curtail* moment. **Promo Mario!** "

The director's voice came off the floor speakers, tired: "Mario, that's not a segment."

"Shhh. It's a *moment.*"

*WAH! He has been the most famous man in his world for so long that he cannot tell the difference between a rescue and a television bit. I used to find this charming. I am rereading it at midnight and I find it terrifying.*

## Part Two: A Name From the Dark Shores

The host's composure lasted one more beat. He clapped his hands, spun in place, and knocked his own chair over with a *clatter*.

"Mamma mia! The suspense is killing me—like when you run out of 1-Up mushrooms in the castle level!" He grabbed both strangers by the shoulders. "Tell-a me, tell-a me—are you from another dimension? Time travelers? Maybe secret Nintendo testers sent to spy on my show?"

Neither answered. Mario spun and began pacing, counting on his fingers.

"I mean, look at this setup—brand new pilot episode filming today! First ever footage of Luigi *playable*, and that cool cutscene where Peach gets kidnapped by Bowser!"

The director yelled, "Action!" Mario snapped into host mode, arms out, teeth bright.

"So what do ya say, folks? Ready to see some gaming history?"

The stranger in the dark clothes did not say anything about gaming history. He said: "I am sorry. I don't really understand."

Mario's grin folded. "Oh no, oh no! Did I go too fast again? Like when you play Super Mario 64 and forget to press Z for camera control?" He lowered the stranger into a director's chair, grabbed a bottle of water from the craft table, and crouched. "Okay, okay. Let me explain slow-like. You fell from *sky-boom*!" He made an explosion shape with both hands. "You landed in the middle of my show's filming day! Nintendo Mania! Pilot episode!"

Technicians moved past with light meters. Somewhere on the far side of the set a microphone *screeched*.

"But don't worry, amigo." He patted the stranger's shoulder. "We'll figure this out together."

The stranger looked at his steward. The steward looked back. Neither looked convinced.

## Part Three: Darian Marsh, and the Man Who Bows

The stranger rose, brushed the dust from his sleeve, and offered a bow that belonged in a throne room rather than a sound stage.

"Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores, at your service. And this here is my steward." He gestured. "Introduce yourself for me, young man."

Mario's eyes went wide — comically, exactly the size they went when he collected one hundred coins in *Mario Bros.* "Darian Marsh?! The Dark Shores?!" He snapped to rigid attention, hands clasped.

The steward stepped forward, hesitated, and bowed the way a soldier bows when he intends to be remembered. "I am Alistair of the Marshkeepers, sworn protector of Lord Darian."

A hush dropped over the set. A technician stopped mid-cable. The director turned slowly from his monitor.

Mario's jaw came open. He removed his red cap and held it over his heart.

"...Mamma mia..." He said it like a prayer and a warning at once. "This—this is bigger than finding all twelve Power Stars..."

*WAH! Twelve. He said twelve. There are twelve Power Stars in that game and I know this because I have had to hear about that game for ten consecutive evenings.
