They swerved into the employee break room: a couch, a coffee machine with a pot still warm, and a wall of security monitors.

"What is the plan, steward?" Darian said. "You are meant to guide me, but it looks like I'm doing all the guiding here."

Alistair straightened, composure returning. "You're right, milord. I should be leading." He scanned the monitors. "We need to find Luigi. And a safe place to wait out the battle. The break room has the cameras—"

"Then break room it is," Darian said. "The other two options were just cornering ourselves."

Four monitors showed different parts of the studio. One showed the battle — evil Mario pinning real Mario to the floor, purple energy crackling around his fists.

And on [[prop:prop_studio_security_footage|Camera Three]], near the prop room, a figure in green and blue was hiding behind crates. Green cap. Blue overalls. Terrified but unharmed.

"No, no, no," Darian said. "That is NOT Luigi. Look closer."

Alistair leaned in. The figure's hat was the wrong shade. Too tall. Too still. And its edges — he would swear to it later — flickered, once, like a screen losing signal.

The figure turned its head sharply. Where Luigi's face should have been, there were two hollow black eyes.

Neither of them was in the same room as that camera. The one in the room reached through the monitor and waited.

"That thing isn't him," Alistair said, and put his hand on Darian's arm. "Don't go there."

The three remaining monitors went to static. All four — together, in sequence — showed the black question mark inside the circle.

Then the coffee machine went cold.

*WAH! So: the report on the front page that morning — the one I filed, the one with the souvenirs and the handsome farewell — ends with a portal. The full account ends with a camera watching two people through a monitor, a missing brother, an evil version of the most famous hero in the world, and a question mark that keeps showing up at every bad turn like a signature. I did not file a newspaper this morning. I filed a trailer. The archive has been quoting a trailer all day. WAH.*

aftermath:
Standing as of 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — per the full account, not the newspaper.

- The portal machine never opened. Darian and Alistair remained in the Hollywood studio, the devices red, Dr. Takeda promising recalibration over days.
- Luigi was reported missing from the studio after the unsupervised tape played. No note, no struggle, no usable security footage.
- A hostile figure calling itself a version of Mario emerged from a television, challenged the host to beat it or perish, and engaged him on the set. Its fate is unreported.
- The Wario Apparition, which seized the studio systems and ran a game-show segment, dissolved after a Wario Inc. tablet was used as a flashlight. The tablet still works. Waluigi is not sorry.
- The 955 BF tape, the funeral footage, the drowning image and the question-mark cipher remain unaccounted for.
- Darian, Alistair, Mario and Dr. Takeda remain the account's only sources. No publisher, no original film and no independent witness has been produced.

name: The Roll Call at Trinity
title: The Roll Call at Trinity: A New Advisor, Eleven Names, and the Word Nobody Was Supposed to Explain
date: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — morning, Classroom 2-B, Trinity General School, Kivotos (Kivotos academy clock)
status: Filed — the class is introduced, the SCHALE attachment is disclosed, the Equestrian liaison breach is admitted and under internal query, and the deployment briefing for Sectors 7 through 12 is unfinished
summary: A new advisor took Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School and ran a roll call, and the roll call turned into the archive's first look inside Kivotos. Eleven students answered to their names: the one who arrived first and claimed the front desk, the one with the chocolate, the one who quieted the room without raising her voice, the one in the corner who is classified supplementary, the one who finished page six of the pamphlet, the one who found gaps in the documentation overnight, the one in the back row with weapons clearance, the one who kept asking what words meant, the one who declared himself lord of the classroom, and the one who admitted nobody had ever explained any of this to him. Asked a direct question, the advisor confirmed the class is attached to SCHALE, spelled the acronym out, conceded it sounds stupid, and explained what it does. A follow-up question about an Equestrian liaison seen walking the school produced an admission that a diplomatic programme had been mishandled. A question about weapons produced a refusal — and the public disclosure of one student's existing clearance. No combat, no travel, no casualties. Eleven people were introduced and one institution said out loud what it wants from them.
description:
*Waluigi was not in this room and has never been to Kivotos, which has not stopped him before. What follows is assembled from the classroom record of a single morning at [Trinity General School](#/article/trinity_general_school), and Waluigi files it because of what it is: an intake. Eleven children, one advisor, and the moment an institution stopped pretending it was a school.*

*[Kivotos](#/article/kivotos) is not new to this archive. It is where [Remi Akamatsu](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was born — Residential District Seven, 12th Harvestide 1026 BF — it is the issuer of the credits in her field wallet, and its four-term academic year has been sitting in the archive's calendar data the whole time. What the archive has never had is an interior. Now it has one, and it is a classroom with a sliding door and a contested front row.*

*Nothing is fought here. Waluigi wants that stated plainly, because the temptation with an introductions session is to apologise for it. Do not. This is the filing where the cast gets their names, the seating chart turns out to be politics, and a man with a clipboard answers a question he could have dodged.*
imageCaption: Classroom 2-B on the morning of the new advisor's first roll call: the sliding door, the window row, the contested front desk, and the back row that behaves like a separate country.

sections.name: I. The Door Slides Open
sections.imageCaption: Ten seconds before anyone else had processed that the door had opened: both palms down on the advisor's desk, the pencil holder still rattling, the halo spinning like a top.
sections.overview:
The door slides rather than swings, and it opened with a click that the record calls satisfying. The new advisor stepped through it adjusting a pair of glasses that — the record is specific — he does not need for vision.

**"Alright everyone, settle down! I'm your new advisor — you can call me Sensei. Think of me as… the glue holding this whole operation together."**

He spun around once and pointed at nothing in particular. Then he laid out the deal: follow the rules, behave like proper students, everything goes smoothly. *We cool?*

The answers arrived in the order that tells you the room. From the window seats, a hand straight up and a grin: **"Sensei~! So does this mean you'll be around to chat during break too?"** From the front row, hair tucked behind an ear and a warm, formal welcome, with the Sisterhood Club's help offered before anyone had asked for it.

And then the door again, because [Misono Mika](#/article/misono_mika) had not finished arriving. She came through roughly ten seconds before the rest of the class had processed that anything was happening, pink hair bouncing, skidded to a halt at the advisor's desk and slammed both palms down on it hard enough to rattle the pencil holder.

**"SENSEI! I got here first! Does that mean I'm your favorite student now~?"**

Her halo spun above her head like an excited top. Behind her, other students were still filing in; Mika had already claimed the desk directly opposite his and sat down in it with a very deliberate, princess-like posture — back straight, hands folded, chin slightly elevated.

Then she offered him tea.

**"Also I brought you tea! Well… I didn't bring tea. But I *thought* about bringing tea."** A pause. **"…The thought counts."**

Somewhere in the middle of this, a newcomer turned to the person in the next seat and asked, with feeling, whether this was really the right place. The answer came back cheerful and immediate: yes, definitely, Mika-senpai does this with every new teacher, and you will get used to it after — *oh, probably never, actually.*

The advisor noticed the whispering, raised an eyebrow, and turned back to the room with a smirk.

**"Something to share? Because if you're comparing me to your last advisor who 'mysteriously disappeared,' I assure you — I'm much harder to get rid of."**

He tapped the desk twice with a knuckle. **"So! Roll call. Let's see who actually shows up on time."**
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi wishes to flag the throwaway line, because throwaway lines are where institutions confess. *Your last advisor who mysteriously disappeared.* He said it as a joke, in air quotes, on his first morning, to eleven children who did not laugh. Nobody in the room asked a follow-up question. Waluigi is asking it: what happened to the last advisor of Classroom 2-B, and why is the replacement already making jokes about it?

sections.name: II. Eleven Names Off a Clipboard
sections.overview:
He picked up the clipboard and read, finger trailing down the page with practiced efficiency, and the roll call did what roll calls do in a first session: it introduced everybody by showing how each of them answers to their own name.

[Kurimura Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) — present, with an enthusiastic little wave.

[Shirasu Azusa](#/article/shirasu_azusa) — silence, then a tiny voice from the corner mumbling something inaudible. *I'll take that as a yes.* Her desk is in the far corner, angled slightly away from the room, as far from everyone else as a desk can be while still being a desk. Her posture was immaculate, her hands folded, her pen aligned perfectly parallel to her notebook's edge. A breeze from a cracked window pushed a strand of hair across her face. She did not move to fix it.

[Ibaragi Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi) — a sharp intake of breath from the middle row. The advisor glanced up, said nothing, marked a check and moved on. She was hunched in her seat like she was trying to physically shrink, gripping the desk edge hard enough to whiten her knuckles. *I'm here.* Her eyes scanned the room to see who was watching, landed on the advisor looking directly at her, and she flinched and looked away fast.

Somewhere in here, [Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) held out a small wrapped chocolate with both hands. *A little something to start the day off sweetly. You looked like you needed it!* The advisor examined it with exaggerated suspicion for a full three seconds, then ate it. **"Mmh. Not bad."**

[Iochi Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) — a polite nod from the front row.

**"…Shaggy."**

Dead silence. Everyone looked around. The advisor scanned the room slowly and sighed through his nose. **"Alrighty, so we're either missing Shaggy, or he's hiding behind that sleeping kid in the back row."**

A hand rose slowly from behind a desk near the window, where [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) had been crouched low trying to make himself invisible. He stood with his characteristic slouch, green shirt hanging off one shoulder. **"Uh… yo. Present. Like, hi."** His voice cracked on *hi*.

Then the clipboard produced a name the advisor had to squint at. **"…Lord Verity."** He looked around the classroom with genuine curiosity, found nobody obviously matching the description, and his eyes landed on the newcomer sitting right there. One eyebrow arched. **"Huh. You're Lord Verity? …Alright then."** He made a checkmark with a confident flick of the wrist and moved on.

He was wrong, and the correction was not quiet. [Lord Verity](#/article/lord_verity) stood up abruptly, chair scraping loud against the floor. Every head turned.

**"YES I AM LORD VERITY. AND I SHALL BE YOUR MASTER FROM THIS DAY FORWARD — KNEEL BEFORE ME, MORTALS!"**

A beat of stunned silence. Someone in the back coughed. Mika started giggling. Airi covered her mouth. The advisor blinked once, twice, and turned calmly back to his clipboard. **"…Right. Next."**

It still took a second prompt — *sensei what about me!* — before he found the right line and produced the name that had been missed: **"You're… Asa Hanko?"** Curious, not unkind, like tasting an unfamiliar word and deciding how it fits in the mouth.

[Kenzaki Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) did not raise her hand when called. She sat in the back with her arms crossed and her legs kicked up on the desk, dark hair falling across one eye, and let out a low chuckle. *Keheh.* Then she looked away. **"…What a pain."**

[Asagao Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) raised a hand slowly, fingers trembling, and gave a small shy wave. **"I-I'm here… Sensei…"** Barely above a whisper, eyes on the floor, sleeve pulled over the knuckles. **"P-Please take care of me…"**

And near the back, one more student sat without leaning toward anybody — not confused, not excited, simply watching, which in that room made them more noticeable than everyone being loud.

The newcomer's assessment of the whole procedure, filed verbatim: *a lot of students.*
sections.waluigi_note: Eleven names and eleven completely different ways of answering to one. The girl in the corner nods so faintly it barely registers. The boy behind the desk hides until the roll reaches him. One of them announces himself as a lord. One of them apologises for existing. Waluigi has covered war councils with less character in them than this register. The advisor read the list in about four minutes and every one of those four minutes is load-bearing.

sections.name: III. The Room Gets Away From Him
sections.imageCaption: Shouting had failed. She stood up, walked to the front, positioned herself slightly behind his desk, and asked. The record says they complied like dominoes falling.
sections.overview:
Between the roll call and the lesson, the classroom stopped being a classroom.

Airi got up and walked the aisle to the back with a second chocolate, weaving between desks with practiced ease, and slid into the seat next to [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy). *Here you go~ Don't let Sensei see you eating candy during his speech though, okay?* He unwrapped it, put it in his mouth, and slouched lower — as though going sideways would make him less visible.

**"Like… thanks for the chocolate, Airi. You're like, way too nice to me."** Then, leaning in at a volume the record notes was *not remotely quiet enough:* **"Uh… why's Lord Verity acting all weird again? Like, is today a cosmic alignment or something?"** His leg bounced under the desk hard enough to vibrate the furniture.

At the front, the advisor raised the clipboard like a shield.

**"ALRIGHT! SEATS! NOW!"**

The room did not obey. Chairs kept scraping. Mika had somehow ended up sitting on top of her desk rather than in her chair. He pinched the bridge of his nose, exhaled slowly through his teeth, and tried being specific instead of loud:

**"Let me make one thing perfectly clear: I don't care who you are or what club you're in. You sit down, you pay attention, and you behave like students. Not… *whatever* this is."**

His eyes swept the room — Lord Verity mid-pose, Shaggy half-swallowed by his hoodie, Azusa staring at a wall, Mika spinning on her chair for no reason anyone could identify.

From the back row, [Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) watched the whole thing with her chin tilted down and her eyes narrowed to razor slits. She pulled out her phone under the desk, thumb hovering, visibly weighing whether this was worth documenting. **"…What a circus."**

Lord Verity, meanwhile, had escalated. He slammed both fists on the desk hard enough to rattle every pencil within two feet. **"THIS CLASS WILL COME TO ATTENTION OR FACE THE WRATH OF LORD VERITY HIMSELF!"** Airi giggled. Mika kept spinning. Someone in the back row did not look up.

Then [Iochi Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) stood up.

She did not shout. She walked to the front, positioned herself slightly behind the advisor's desk, gave a small nod to the students nearest her — a silent signal — and said, in a voice the record describes as soft but carrying clearly:

**"If everyone could take their seats properly, that would be wonderful~"**

The record: *cutting through the noise more effectively than any shouting ever could. A few students glance her way and begin complying, chairs clicking into place one by one like dominoes falling.*

What finally settled Lord Verity was a last warning: sit down or be removed. His fist was still in the air. The words died on his lips. He lowered the fist slowly, and the hoodie-cape slid off one shoulder and pooled on the desk behind him *like a deflated balloon.*

**"…You can't kick ME out. I'm not even IN anything yet."**

He stood in the middle of the aisle, suddenly looking less like an emperor and more like someone who had wandered into the wrong building. **"…Fine."** Through gritted teeth, jaw tight.

The advisor watched him go back to his seat with the quiet satisfaction of a man who had just defused a bomb using nothing but volume and posture. **"Thank you for your cooperation, Lord Verity."** The sarcasm, the record notes, was *barely thin enough to pass through a colander.*
sections.waluigi_note: Note who actually restored order, because it was not the adult. The advisor shouted twice and got nothing. Mari stood up, asked nicely, and the room folded like wet paper. She has no authority in that room whatsoever. She has something better, which is that everybody likes her and nobody wants to be the one who ignored her. Waluigi has watched generals fail to do what that girl did with one sentence and a hair-tuck.

sections.name: IV. The Word He Did Not Have To Explain
sections.imageCaption: THE RESISTANCE in underlined block capitals, and a rough map of the eastern perimeter — warehouses, supply routes, and abandoned industrial buildings that make good hiding places.
sections.overview:
With the room finally seated, he leaned against the desk and started on what the class actually *is*. Students of Trinity General School. Here to learn, grow, and be prepared for whatever comes next.

**"SCHALE operations, academy life, the whole package."**

And then a voice from the floor: **"SCHALE operations?"**

The session changed shape at that line. [Lord Verity](#/article/lord_verity)'s eyes snapped to attention — *actual* attention, not the theatrical kind. The dramatic pose melted like frost in sunlight. His fingers tightened on the desk edge.

**"Wait. You're saying this class — THIS class — is connected to SCHALE? As in… actual missions? Real-world operations?"**

His voice cracked on *real-world.* The record catches what was underneath the theatrics for exactly one second: *something raw — something hungry. Something that sounds like a kid who's been waiting for exactly this his entire life.* He started to say *I thought we were just—*, stopped himself, swallowed, and put the mask back on. It no longer fit properly.

In the corner, [Azusa](#/article/shirasu_azusa)'s eyes sharpened — the record's simile is *like a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked.* The name landed in her chest and stayed there, heavy and cold. She knows what SCHALE means better than most students at Trinity, because she has felt the weight of systems that sort people into categories they did not choose, into boxes labelled *supplementary* like it is a diagnosis rather than a circumstance.

[Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi) tensed, shoulders to her ears. **"…What does that have to do with ANY of us?"** — sharper than she meant it, which is saying something.

[Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) whispered the word to herself, held the advisor's gaze for exactly two seconds, and said **"I… I know what that is."** Then her courage ran out.

[Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) said what nobody else was willing to: **"Uh… like, yeah. What exactly IS SCHALE? Sounds like some kinda… I dunno, video game thing or whatever?"** And then the sentence that turns this filing from a briefing into an indictment:

**"Like… okay, real talk. I've been at Trinity for a while now and nobody EVER explained this stuff to me. I get that there's Knights, I get that there's the Resistance, I even get that there's some kinda war going on — but 'operations?' Like… combat operations? Because if you're telling me I gotta fight something, I need to know where the nearest exit is first."**

The advisor set the clipboard down with a deliberate click and turned to face the room fully. He held up a hand when Lord Verity opened his mouth. *Nope. I'm talking. You're listening.*

**"SCHALE isn't some secret club or a video game. It stands for Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution."**

He let the acronym sit. Then came the question that got the honest answer — *sounds stupid, what does it actually do?*

**"It does sound stupid. I'll give you that."**

A few nervous laughs. He held up a finger before anyone got comfortable.

**"But here's the thing — it's not really an acronym people throw around for fun. SCHALE is the backbone of everything that keeps this city breathing. It decides which Knights respond to hazards, how resources get allocated, who gets support when things go sideways."**

[Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) translated it for the students too embarrassed to ask, opening with the line that let them off the hook — *most people don't fully understand it until they're told directly* — and laying it out in three clean sentences: the framework that keeps Kivotos stable, coordinating Knight responses and Resistance intelligence, turning strategic decisions into actual missions. *In essence… it's the difference between knowing there's a threat and actually doing something about it.*

Then the whiteboard came out, and with it the geography. Sectors 7 through 12, along Kivotos's eastern perimeter: warehouses, supply routes, a couple of abandoned industrial buildings that make great hiding spots for people who do not want to be found. The Resistance had been spotted moving supply lines through those corridors. Exact numbers unknown.

Asked what any of that meant, he wrote **THE RESISTANCE** on the board in block letters and underlined it twice.

**"They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for — the academies, the peace agreements, all of it."**

He turned around and looked directly at the student who had asked. **"The short version: we're going there because someone's been moving weapons through those sectors, and SCHALE is the group that stops that from happening. You — all of you — are part of that."**
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi is going to be careful here, because this is the paragraph where an archivist earns his keep. *They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for* is not a finding. It is a description of an armed political faction, delivered in one sentence, to a room of children, by an employee of the body they are fighting. It may even be true. Waluigi does not know, and neither does anyone in that classroom, and that is the point: not one student in the room had the information to test it. The archive files it as the advisor's characterisation. Ask again in twenty sessions.

sections.name: V. The Ponies, the Guns, and the Thing He Should Not Have Said
sections.overview:
Two more questions landed before the briefing could resume, and both of them opened something.

The first came almost in passing — a question about external threats versus internal ones, and then: *what about the pony liaison that came from Equestrian earlier, I saw some walking around the school, was that meant to be private?*

The advisor's expression shifted. Just barely, just enough for anyone paying attention. His jaw tightened a fraction. He set the clipboard down on the desk with a deliberate click, and chose his words like stepping over a tripwire he could not see.

**"That's… a separate matter."**

Then he confirmed it: a diplomatic initiative between Kivotos and Canterlot. Small groups, cultural exchange, building goodwill before things get messy enough to need actual military coordination. *It was supposed to be handled quietly.*

He exhaled through his nose.

**"So the fact that you saw them walking around openly tells me someone dropped the ball on security protocols somewhere along the line."** His eyes swept the room. **"I'll look into it. If any of you see more of those liaisons wandering where they shouldn't be, report it to me — not to social media, not to your friends, to me. Directly."**

In the corner, Azusa's pen stopped mid-notation. Two pieces that did not fit: an organisation that runs on need-to-know, and diplomatic personnel walking a school corridor in plain view. She wrote something brief in the margin that was not part of the lecture, said **"…Understood"** to nobody in particular, straightened a page that was already perfectly aligned, and resumed writing.

[Airi](#/article/kurimura_airi) had three questions and no filter: are there snacks in Sector 7, are the ponies friendly, can she hug one, and do they get breaks. [Shaggy](#/article/shaggy) followed with the sensible objection nobody else made — *if we're dealing with bad guys AND ponies showing up uninvited, that's like… two different problems, right?*

It was correct, and the advisor said so. The Resistance is an internal threat operating out of Kivotos itself. The Equestrian liaisons are an external diplomatic situation *that someone mishandled* — his tone carrying an edge that suggested opinions about who. **"The fact that those two things intersected at this school without proper coordination is exactly why SCHALE exists."**

On the ponies, he was blunt: they are not your friends, they are diplomatic personnel operating under an agreement *that does NOT include hugging.*

Then the second question: **"We can all use guns at least right?"**

The silence lasted exactly two seconds before [Tsurugi](#/article/kenzaki_tsurugi) spoke, and she did not look at whoever had asked. She kept her eyes on the advisor. She uncrossed her arms slowly, deliberately, leaned forward, and pointed at him like a blade.

**"…Seriously? If you're about to say 'yes' to that, then this class is just an excuse for a shooting range and I'm filing paperwork."** Her expression hardened. **"I've handled weapons since before most of you were old enough to stop putting them in your mouths."**

She leaned back, arms recrossing with finality. **"Sensei. What's the actual plan?"**

Shaggy put himself on the record immediately and defensively — *I just want it on the record that I said nothing about wanting guns* — describing himself and Scooby as diplomatic solution kind of guys, and offering a bag of Scooby Snacks as his contribution to the mission.

The advisor exhaled slowly through his nose.

**"Nobody is handing out guns."**

Stone-cold finality. The room went quiet for exactly one second. And then he held up a finger to preempt an objection Tsurugi had not made and did not appear about to make.

**"—except Tsurugi. You already have clearance."** A beat. **"Everyone else: no."**

He turned back to the whiteboard and wrote **need-to-know** in block letters, underlining it twice: SCHALE tells you what you need for your assignment, and you do not ask about things outside it. Anyone whose role requires a firearm will be briefed separately, with proper safety training, by certified personnel. *Not me. Not YouTube.*
sections.waluigi_note: He disclosed a student's weapons clearance to ten of her classmates in order to win an argument he had already won. She had not volunteered it. She had, in fact, just spent her only real contribution of the session arguing AGAINST arming children — which is the most responsible position anybody takes in this entire filing, and it is taken by the girl with her boots on the furniture. The record does not show her reacting. Waluigi finds that the most informative non-reaction of the morning, and notes for the file that the man explaining need-to-know had, ninety seconds earlier, told the room something it did not need to know.

sections.name: VI. Cute Outfits, and the Question He Did Not Answer
sections.overview:
What the class did with all of this was form a committee about clothes.

It started when he said there would be no cool gadgets and no matching outfits — *at least… not yet* — and let it hang. That was a mistake. **"not yet! does that mean we get cool outfits!"**

Airi nearly knocked over a juice box getting out of her seat. **"WE'RE GETTING OUTFITS?! Oh my gosh oh my gosh—"** What colour, what style, matching or pick-your-own, and could hers have chocolate mint on it somehow.

From the back row, Tsurugi's mouth twitched upward — not quite a smile, the precursor to one. **"…Not yet, huh. How long do we have to wait? …Days? Weeks?"** Low, direct, two syllables cutting through the noise.

[Yoshimi](#/article/ibaragi_yoshimi)'s eye twitched. **"…Outfits?"** — said as though he had announced they would be dissecting cats. **"If this is about uniforms, I'm opting out. I don't do group matching. Last time the school made me wear anything I looked like a kid playing dress-up."** She looked sideways at Airi's bouncing with the expression of someone watching a person pour gasoline on themselves, and asked how much of the actual briefing Airi was hearing. Airi was not hearing a single word. Yoshimi exhaled through her nose like a frustrated bull.

The advisor tried to reclaim it. The outfits comment was a joke. *Mostly.* SCHALE is not glamorous — it is paperwork and logistics and making sure the right people are in the right places when things go wrong. **"But it IS important. The Resistance runs through this system. Every Knight deployment, every supply line, every evacuation order during a hazard event — it all flows through SCHALE."**

In the corner, Azusa delivered her verdict flat, like reporting a weather condition. **"Cute outfits. …Who cares about outfits."** A barely perceptible shrug. And then the question underneath the entire session:

**"The question is whether SCHALE actually works. Or if it's just another thing that sounds important but doesn't do anything for people who are already at the bottom of every list."**

Her gaze dropped to her desk — notebook closed, pen aligned parallel to its edge.

**"…Doesn't matter though. I'm not on any list. Supplementary students don't count for much either way."**

Nobody answered her.

The committee formed anyway, and it formed around the newcomer, who had declared a preference for cute clothes and recruited Airi on the spot. Lord Verity, whose hoodie Airi had been modelling as a ball gown without permission, rose to bless the arrangement — *BEHOLD! The Lord of Verity graces this humble girl—* — while Airi waved and mouthed THANKS with exaggerated enthusiasm, and he pivoted mid-sentence into *an alliance that shakes the very FOUNDATIONS of… SCHALE training readiness!* He pointed at the advisor, retracted, pointed again but lower, then settled for crossing his arms and nodding sagely.

Yoshimi watched it with an expression the record says could curdle milk. **"An alliance. They're forming an *alliance* over a cape."** Then, flatly: **"…I'm not joining any alliance."** And then, in the very next breath: **"But if Sensei needs someone who actually reads the handouts…"**

She pulled a crumpled SCHALE pamphlet from her bag and slapped it on the desk with more force than necessary.

**"I finished page six."**

[Hanae](#/article/asagao_hanae) raised her hand hesitantly, like asking permission to speak at a town hall. **"…I want to join the alliance too."** She introduced herself properly, said she does not do loud things, and offered logistics and scheduling — paperwork stuff. Then she held up a small notebook filled with neat handwriting and colour-coded tabs.

**"I already started organizing the SCHALE information Sensei shared. There were gaps in the documentation so I cross-referenced it with the school's emergency protocols…"**

Nobody had asked her to. It had been a matter of hours. She found gaps.

The newcomer's response to the offer of paperwork was *what no eww* and a counter-proposal to design cute outfits for the class instead — and Hanae, who by every expectation should have folded, lit up instead *like someone just turned on a lamp inside her chest cavity.* She offered to help pick colours and check uniform modifications against school regulations, trailed off when she heard herself volunteering detailed logistical support for a committee that did not exist, and went pink at the ears. **"…I'll do whatever helps!"**

Airi called her a genius and a hidden treasure, grabbed her hands and shook them gently. Hanae looked startled and did not pull away.

Then Airi turned the whole thing on the least approachable person in the room: they would make everyone look so good that even Kenzaki could not complain. Group photos. Props. Maybe balloons.

**"…You want to put BALLOONS on SCHALE tactical gear."**

**"It would LOOK SO CUTE—"**

Tsurugi stared at her for a long, uncomfortable beat. Then — so quietly the record says it almost did not exist — the corner of her mouth twitched.

**"Keheh."**

Airi screamed with joy.

And in the middle of all of it, [Mari](#/article/iochi_mari) raised her hand, though she had already been looking at him, and asked the only question that went to the point:

**"I think what everyone here is actually asking — underneath all the outfit requests and snack searches — is whether SCHALE means we'll get to DO something meaningful. People don't care about gadgets or uniforms. They care about purpose. So… will it?"**

The record does not show him answering.

He dropped into his chair with the bone-tired slump of a man who had survived a natural disaster and was now filling out paperwork about it, observed that nobody had mentioned the classroom would treat every meeting like a variety show, and set the order of business: deployment rotation first. Then fashion.

The word came out, the record says, *like he's chewing glass.*
sections.waluigi_note:
Two questions were asked in this room and neither was answered. Azusa asked whether the system does anything for people at the bottom of every list, and said, out loud, that she is not on any list. Mari asked whether any of this amounts to purpose. Eleven people and one adult heard both. The reply to the first was silence and the reply to the second was a deployment rotation.

Waluigi is going to drop the voice for a moment, because this is the part that matters and the jokes can wait. An institution that will not answer *does this do anything for me* has told you the answer. The archive will be asking both questions again, in writing, every session, until somebody in that building says something.

outcome:
No combat, no travel, no casualties, and nothing physically changed hands except two chocolates and a crumpled pamphlet. What changed is what the class knows.

Filed as settled: Classroom 2-B is attached to SCHALE operations; the acronym is Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution; the body coordinates Knight deployments, resource allocation and hazard response, and runs on need-to-know. A deployment rotation covering Sectors 7 through 12 on Kivotos's eastern perimeter is in preparation, justified by reported Resistance movement of weapons and supply lines. The class will not be armed; one student already is.

Filed as admitted: an Equestrian liaison programme with Canterlot exists, was intended to be conducted quietly, and was observed by students walking the school openly. The advisor characterised this as a failure of security protocol and opened an internal query.

Filed as open: what happened to the previous advisor of Classroom 2-B, referred to in a joke as having 'mysteriously disappeared'. Whether SCHALE does anything for students classified supplementary. Whether any of this amounts to purpose — asked directly, and not answered.

aftermath:
**Eleven students have names in the archive and one institution has stated its terms.** That is the whole of it, and for an intake filing it is enough.

The alliance that formed over an oversized hoodie is, on paper, an outfit-design committee: Asa Hanko proposing, Airi escalating, Hanae supplying logistics, Lord Verity blessing it, Yoshimi refusing to join while volunteering to do the reading. It has no standing and no remit. It is also the only structure in that classroom that anybody chose.

The deployment briefing did not finish. Sectors 7 through 12 are named, the Resistance is characterised, and the rotation itself is still unread when the record ends.

Three things are owed. The previous advisor of Classroom 2-B is unaccounted for and was joked about on the replacement's first morning. The Equestrian liaison breach is under an internal query with no stated deadline. And Shirasu Azusa said, in a full classroom, that supplementary students do not count for much either way, and nobody contradicted her.
waluigiAssessment:
**The session is an introduction and the disclosure is an accident.** Waluigi wants both halves of that sentence taken seriously.

The advisor came in to run a roll call and set expectations. What he actually did was answer a question a confused student asked because they did not know it was the kind of question you are supposed to already know the answer to. And once he started answering he did not stop: the acronym, the function, the sectors, the Resistance, the ponies, the clearance. A more careful man lets the first SCHALE question die in the noise. Waluigi has covered enough institutions to say that the careful man is the more common one, and to note, grudgingly, that this one is better than that.

But look at what the honesty cost. He told a room of children that the people in the eastern sectors are criminals who want to tear it all down, in one sentence, with no evidence offered and none available to them. He confirmed a diplomatic programme was being run badly by confirming that seeing it was the problem. And he named a student's weapons clearance out loud, to ten classmates, moments before writing NEED-TO-KNOW on a whiteboard and underlining it twice.

The children, meanwhile, sorted themselves faster than any institution could have. Mika took the front. Tsurugi took the back and watched only him. Azusa angled her desk toward the door. Airi crossed the room twice to reach whoever was alone. Mari stood up and stopped a riot by asking politely. Hanae went home and audited the documentation. Yoshimi read page six and waited all session for a reason to say so.

And Lord Verity, who had spent the morning demanding that mortals kneel, said *I'm not even IN anything yet*, and then heard the word SCHALE and forgot to perform.

**Waluigi's finding:** this is a good room. It is also a room where a fourteen-year-old said she is not on any list and eleven people let it pass. Waluigi has filed that in two places so it cannot be lost. WAH.

description:
Waluigi is going to open this filing with the only sentence in the whole account that behaves like an exit, because nothing else in the building did.

**A button beside a coffee machine said EMERGENCY EXIT, and pressing it made coffee. Everything after that — the vent, the song, the fire, the ice, the word, the curtains, the man with the remote — followed from a lord deciding to climb anyway.**

## The break room, inventoried

This filing continues [the promo filing](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/promo_mario_newspaper) without a break: [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) and [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) in the employee break room, four monitors showing static and one showing a lie, the coffee machine gone cold, and the sound of a corrupted [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) beating the real one somewhere out in the corridors. How do we get out of here, though — we have no other leads but this place. Right.

[Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) surveyed the room like the steward he is. A back door leading to the kitchen. An air vent big enough to crawl through. The monitors, showing possible exits. And something new: a small button by the coffee machine, labelled **EMERGENCY EXIT**.

*WAH! New. A button that was not there before, in a building that keeps adding rooms to its own script. Waluigi has filed entire investigations that began with less.*

## The button that made coffee

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) pressed it, with the specific pessimism of a man testing whether the exit is another trap — *brilliant, let's see how it's not an exit to the coffee machine.*

The coffee machine came to life. Aggressively. Scalding coffee poured out uncontrollably; the room filled with steam; [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) coughed out the sentence *it's… not an exit* — and then the steam did what steam does. It rose. And a ceiling vent popped open from the heat.

The exit was the coffee machine's fault. The building had hidden an escape route behind an appliance, or the appliance had staged a rescue — in this studio those are the same sentence with different fonts.

## Into the ceiling

They armed themselves from the break room like men who have learned what this place does to the unarmed: [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) took a heavy metal rolling pin and the broken coffee-pot handle with its sharp edge. [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) shut off the machine, the steam cleared, and he boosted his lord up into the duct first.

The vent was dark, dusty, cramped — hands and knees, faint emergency light from below, small cracks letting in glow. Something scurried past [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s face. A rat. An ordinary rat, which after the black-eyed thing on Camera Three was almost reassuring. [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) fumbled for the rolling pin; the metal clanged against the duct walls, one long echo rolling through the whole system, and [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) whispered the sentence this archive would like bronzed: *careful — noise might draw attention.*

Ahead: a faint blue light.

## The man at the blue light

The vent opened over a maintenance room with a working computer screen, and below it, someone typing fast, muttering *come on… come ON…*

It was [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi). Alive. Alone. His face lit blue, exhausted but unharmed. On the screen: security camera feeds, a map of the studio, and notes headed **Wario's corruption**. He typed that he had to find Mario, that he had to fix this — a scared brother running his own investigation two rooms away from the fight, with better tools than the archive has ever had and nobody to tell.

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) watched from the vent and shushed [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) — *let's see if he does anything rash; we don't know how dangerous he is.* It is the correct instinct in this building and Waluigi has said so in ink. The archive has already filed one [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) that was not [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi). The man at the blue light zoomed cameras, checked door sensors, typed notes, seemed normal — and then grabbed a flashlight and stood up to leave.

## The rolling pin, and the arm that stopped it

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) went for the drop — out of the vent, rolling pin coming down on the head of a man he had decided not to trust.

[Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper)'s hand closed on his arm mid-swing. The steward stopped his own lord's kill shot on a hunch, and the hunch was right, and it was also nearly fatal for everybody: [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) turned, saw an armed stranger descending from his ceiling, and did exactly what a cornered man does. He dodged the second swing and put the flashlight into [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s shoulder hard enough to numb it. [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) shouted that they were not here to hurt him. [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) was not listening. He was in full panic, ready to fight or flee or scream.

*WAH! Two minutes of surveillance undone by one rolling pin. In the margin of the account Waluigi has written: the steward earns his keep twice in this filing, and the second time is not this.*

## Innocence doesn't get you far

The door went off its hinges.

[Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) stood in it — bruised, grinning, glowing red-eyed, fresh from beating the real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) somewhere out in the corridors. *Innocence doesn't get you far,* he said, surveying the room like a man reading a seating chart. Three against one, [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) counted. *We can take him… I think.*

They could not. [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) moved like a special effect — dodged the flashlight, dodged the rolling pin, shoved [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) into a desk, laughed the whole time, and hurled [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) into a shelf by the collar. What actually landed was [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s rolling pin: a full swing, **CLANG**, into the shoulder, the first honest hit anyone has put on this thing in two filings. [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) grunted, stumbled back — surprised — and for one second the room believed.

They pressed it. [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) kicked his legs. [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), battered upright, called *GO FOR HIS FACE!* — and [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh), somewhere in the noise, produced the sentence that Waluigi will now have to live with:

**"A king cannot let his subjects fall!"**

The lord of the Dark Shores and his steward hit the corrupted Mario together and put him through the computer desk. Monitors shattered. And then the floor began to shake, and [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) started to laugh again, and standing up out of the wreckage he wore a cape.

## The cape

Not a costume cape. A cape of **shadowy, pixelated feathers**, moving unnaturally, like a living thing — and the shaking, the flickering lights, the cracking walls were coming from it. The cape was the power source. [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) said it out loud: his weakness, it has to be. Destroy the cape.

Then the floor fell in.

All three of them dropped into the collapse — and three **paratroopas in studio uniforms with parachutes** caught them by the arms out of the air. Studio crew. Parachute rigs. One yelled *HOLD ON TIGHT.* [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) screamed below, cheated of three victims at once.

*WAH! Waluigi has questions and he is going to put all of them in the investigation file, starting with: since when does a television studio keep a paratroopa rescue squad, and who wrote them into the budget?*

## Plumber Man

The paratroopas did not fly the party out. They flew it **at** [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) — a flying squad in formation, weapons drawn, non-lethal rounds aimed at the cape. *NEUTRALIZE THE THREAT.*

And the studio turned the music on.

**Plumber Man** is filed in full in the [songbook](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/songs) with the lyrics as sung, because what happened next cannot be filed without it: [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) began to fight to the beat. Dodging on the downbeat. Backflips on the chorus. A villain in a feather cape, dancing through a tranq barrage in perfect time while the paratroopas — who train for many things — could not get their timing to land.

[Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) covered his ears, then stopped covering them. He knew the song. He hummed it, weakly, unwillingly, drawn to it — and the account reaches the conclusion the archive also reached: **the song belongs to the real Mario.** Four feet ten, the stache, the star that powers him, the pipes, the lass, the kingdom. It is a love song disguised as a jingle, and the corrupted copy of the man was using it as a weapon.

At the final note, [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) appeared behind him. Bruised. Hat askew. Crawled out of the wreckage on his own. The paratroopas gasped *Sir, you're alive*; [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) nearly wept; and the real and the corrupted stood face to face while the song faded.

## The freeze, and the yank

Four against one now — *still not scared*, [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) said, and cracked his neck, and the fight resumed. [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) ordered the charge — and [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) stopped. Mid-motion. Head tilted, eyes flickering like a screen losing signal, the cape's dark feathers starting to fray. A gust came off it that knocked papers, equipment, and finally [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway like a ragdoll. The paratroopas caught [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) and [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) by the arms and anchored to a broken pipe.

Then the statue came back to life and hit the real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) across the face hard enough to put him through a wall, and it was clear the fight was lost — until the lord of the Dark Shores remembered what he is for.

**"As a king, I order the troops into formation — a V, like a bird."**

The squad snapped into a V. The V cut the wind. And on the next order — *grab Luigi, fly him into that cape* — the lead paratroopa took [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) into the formation's dive, straight at the fraying feathers, and [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi), who came to this studio to find his brother, reached out with both hands and **yanked the cape off.**

[Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) screamed.

## A leaf, a second head, and a very stupid return

The scream became a smile. In his hand: a **tanuki leaf**. The transformation ran through him — fox tail, [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario)'s wild hair, and then, grotesque on his shoulder, **a second head: [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario)'s**, grinning.

And through the broken window behind them came [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) — blown away minutes ago, presumed lost — crashing back in covered in dust, carrying a **flaming pipe**, with visible rage and, in [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh)'s own words, a plan this filing can only describe as *really stupid.* The Wario head popped off like a balloon and burst into smoke, as if it agreed.

The flaming pipe met the tanuki tail. The leaf caught fire. [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) tackled the thing off its feet, and [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) snatched the burning leaf out of the air just as it fully ignited.

## Fire, water, ice

The corrupted Mario ran out of forms to wear and put on the last one: he **erupted into fire** — no shape left, a living blaze, the room catching around him. [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) looked for a fire alarm, found one red and smashed-glassed by the shattered door, and went for it through the heat on his belly — *it's too risky, but I must keep going* — debris under his hands, a flame whip missing him by inches. He smashed the glass and pulled the handle.

Sprinklers. Water everywhere. The fire form hissed, shrank, flickered. [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) looked at his hands — soot, scratches, small burns. Alive.

And [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) pointed at the dying fire, and the room turned **cold**. Frost climbed the walls, breath turned visible, the sprinkler water became icicles, and the corrupted Mario stood remade as a body of shimmering blue ice with glowing eyes. The real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) punched it and his fist froze stuck in the surface.

*How many forms does this thing have?* [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) said — and answered himself: **this must be all an act.**

The ice sculpture smirked. Which is how they knew he was right.

## CUT

Here is the moment the filing exists for, and Waluigi wants it quoted exactly, because it is the moment a provincial lord out-reasoned an entire television studio with one word.

**"CUT!"**

Everything stopped. The ice stopped spreading. The paratroopas lowered their weapons mid-breath. The real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) lowered his fists *like he just remembered something* — and [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario)'s frozen expression flickered, pixelated, broke apart like a bad signal. The word had reached whatever was running the show, and whatever was running the show **flinched.**

Theatrical curtains — heavy velvet, whole-ceiling — came down from above. Crew voices. Equipment moving. Someone shouting *cut the feed.* The curtains closed with a THUD, and when they opened again the studio had reset itself: the original break room, no flames, no ice, no evil copies — [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh), [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), the real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario), and a single television showing static. *What just happened?* [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) asked. Nobody had it.

*WAH! He said the word the building lives in fear of. Not a spell, not a weapon — a PRODUCTION COMMAND. Waluigi has been filing this place as a trap for two filings and it may in fact be a stage that cannot bear to be told the take is over.*

## Best show on TV

[Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) walked in clapping, and applause came out of the dark.

*Bravo! What an entertaining performance!* Oscar-worthy, he said — the ice scene, brilliant special effects — and an audience that was not there roared approval while a television replayed the fight as security footage. He admitted all of it with his arms spread: *Best show on TV!* Some of you didn't sign up for it. The real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) asked the only question that mattered — *you used me? Like some kind of puppet?* — and [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) waved it off as a bit of fun.

And [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh), who has spent two filings learning to check this building's work, looked at the audience.

**Every seat was empty.**

Beyond the seats, through the windows, the whole studio facility: silent. No crew, no life, nobody. The applause was a recording for a room of chairs. *We're alone,* [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario) said, and [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario)'s smirk finally faltered, and four men who had just survived his variety hour began to close on him with their sleeves rolled.

## The man Wario bows to

They never got to him. A voice behind them said, *since this was all for show, let's see how you like the real deal* — and there stood a figure in a **director's cap**, holding a script.

[Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario)'s face went pale and he bowed. *Boss.*

**[Director Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/director_mario)** — and Waluigi is filing that name exactly as the account gives it, cold, calculating, no warmth in him anywhere. The corrupted Mario was an actor. The song was a number. [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) was the producer. The Director said the show had gone over better than [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) knew, that he knew about the results, and then said the quiet part with his cigar snapping in half in his fingers: *you tried to f*** me.*

He took [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) by the collar, put him through a wall hard enough to shake the building, told him *you betrayed me — you ruined MY show,* and knocked him unconscious with one punch. Then he straightened his suit like a man who had swatted a fly, looked once — unreadably — at [Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh), [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper), [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi) and the real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario), and walked out without a word.

## The watcher, the hall, and the remote

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) — alone — noticed that [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) was still there. Half in shadow, perfectly still, red eyes tracking the Director to the door. He told nobody. He moved for the exit slowly, signalled [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper) to look, and let the whole room arrive at its own stillness around the thing in the corner.

And [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario) smiled. Slowly. And raised one finger, and pointed — not at any of them — at the door the Director had left through.

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh) stepped out into the dim hallway and waited, and heavy deliberate footsteps came on, and he hid in a dark alcove, and **[Director Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/director_mario) walked past him close enough to touch.** In one hand: a folder. In the other, carried with the ease of long habit, a **small remote device with buttons and wires running from it.**

A control unit. For [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario). Or for the whole studio. The account ends on the thought the archive now cannot put down: *that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.*

## Standing

[Darian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lord_darian_marsh): burned hands, a numb shoulder, a working rolling pin, and the only complete picture of what this studio actually is. [Alistair](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/alistair_marshkeeper): blown the length of a hallway and back through a window with a flaming pipe, unkillable and unconsulted. [Luigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/luigi): found alive, his notes on Wario's corruption on a studio computer, his brother's song stuck in his head. The real [Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/mario): beaten, frozen, unfrozen, and standing. [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario): unconscious on his own soundstage, disciplined by his own employer. [Evil Mario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/evil_mario): alive, unwearied, and pointing at the man with the remote. And the Director: gone round a corner with a folder, a control unit, and every answer this file has wanted since a newspaper said PROMO MARIO.

The applause was for nobody. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.

WAH.
outcome: The escape attempt became a raid on the show itself. The studio's exits are still traps, but the ceiling was real, the paratroopas are real crew, and Luigi — reported missing since the promo account — was found alive at the maintenance computer with notes on Wario's corruption. The cape of pixelated feathers was destroyed by a V-formation pass and Luigi's hands; the corrupted Mario burned through a tanuki leaf, a second Wario head, fire, and ice before the word CUT froze the entire production and the curtains came down. Evil Mario survived everything and pointed the survivors at the Director's exit. In the hallway, hidden, Darian saw the Director carry past him a folder and a small wired remote — a control unit for Evil Mario, or the studio, or both. Nobody has the remote. The archive now knows the show has an off switch and an owner.

reputationNotes._record: No standing moved: the studio is not a faction, its paratroopas take no orders the archive can bill, and the only institution on the stage answers to a man the archive met four paragraphs ago.

aftermath:
**The show has a director.** Director Mario — a cold copy of the most famous face in the world — outranks Wario inside the studio, and Wario found out by going through a wall.

**The applause was for nobody.** Every seat was empty; the whole facility was silent. Whatever audience the show plays to, it was never in the room.

**Evil Mario is an actor with a power source** — pixelated feather cape, destroyed; tanuki leaf, burned; fire, sprinkled; ice, CUT. He survived all of it, and pointed the survivors at the Director's exit.

**Luigi is alive**, at a studio computer, holding notes on Wario's corruption — the best evidence the file has ever been handed.

**The remote exists.** Small, buttoned, wired, carried like a habit by a man who no longer knows he was seen with it. A control unit for Evil Mario, or the whole studio.

**Unresolved:** who Director Mario answers to; what the folder holds; whether the paratroopas take orders from the remote or the Director; what Evil Mario wants; and how a lord of the Dark Shores gets a wired remote off the most dangerous man in the building.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The word did what the weapons could not.** Two filings of violence — fireballs, javelins, warhammers, rolling pins — and the thing that stopped the corrupted Mario dead was a production command delivered by a provincial lord who had worked out the building's grammar. CUT is not a spell. It is a word the studio's owner could not afford to have said in front of the cast. Waluigi has re-shelved half of this file accordingly: the question is no longer how to beat Evil Mario. The question is who is afraid of the word CUT, and why.

**2. The remote is the whole case.** A folder and a small wired device, carried past a hidden witness by a man who had just demonstrated what he does to employees who exceed their brief. If it runs Evil Mario, it explains the cape, the leaf, the fire, the ice — a costume rack with a controller. If it runs the STUDIO, it explains the resetting break room, the curtains, the applause with no audience, and the exits that lie. Either way, the Mario disappearance file now has an object to hunt instead of a vibe.

**3. Luigi was doing the archive's job better than the archive.** Security feeds, a studio map, notes on Wario's corruption, and a mission statement — find Mario, fix this — while Waluigi was filing newspapers. The maintenance computer is the best evidence in this case and it is sitting in a building that resets itself. Somebody should go back for it.

**4. The empty seats are the part Waluigi cannot file yet.** A show needs an audience. The applause track says one exists. The room says it does not. Either the audience is somewhere the windows do not show, or the performance is being recorded for a viewer the building is not prepared to name. Both readings have a person at the end of them, and Waluigi has a name he is not writing down until he has to.

**Recommendation:** the remote, before the Director notices it was seen. And somebody collect Luigi's notes on the way out.

WAH.

entries.beat: The fall onto the pilot set
entries.detail: Darian and Alistair drop out of their own sky onto a soundstage mid-shoot: the tour, the product demonstration, the tape, the game show, the flashlight. Filed as the promo account — the teaser this timeline's day began with.
Alistair surveys like the steward he is: back door to the kitchen, an air vent, five monitors, a cold coffee machine — and a small button labelled EMERGENCY EXIT that was not there before.
Darian presses it with calibrated pessimism. Scalding coffee, a room filling with steam — and the rising heat pops a ceiling vent open. The exit was the appliance's fault.
A rolling pin, a broken coffee-pot handle, the machine shut off, and a steward's cuped hands: the king goes into the duct first.

entries.detail: Evil Mario, fresh from beating the real Mario, reads the seating chart: innocence doesn't get you far. The room loses the arithmetic — until a rolling pin finds a shoulder, CLANG, the first honest hit in two filings, and a king declares he cannot let his subjects fall.

entries.beat: The cape, the floor, the squad
entries.detail: The pixelated feather cape is the power source; the floor falls in; three studio-uniform paratroopas catch them out of the air — a rescue squad on payroll, and Waluigi has questions about the budget.

entries.span: one complete performance — 3:41 by the archive's copy
entries.detail: The studio turns the music on and the actor fights to the beat: dodges on the downbeat, backflips on the chorus, a tranq barrage that cannot find its timing. Luigi covers his ears, then stops. He knows the song. It belongs to his brother.
Bruised, hat askew, crawled out of the wreckage on his own. Sir, you're alive. The real and the corrupted stand face to face while the song runs out.

entries.span: one gust; then minutes filed as MISSING
entries.detail: The copy stops mid-motion, the cape frays, and the gust knocks Alistair clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway. The paratroopas anchor the others to a broken pipe.
A king cannot let his subjects fall, so he orders the troops into a V, like a bird. The V cuts the wind; Luigi rides the dive and yanks the cape off with both hands. The actor screams.

entries.span: a minute, and a really stupid plan
entries.beat: A leaf, a second head, a window
entries.detail: A tanuki leaf: fox tail, Wario's hair, a second grinning Wario head on one shoulder. Through the broken window comes Alistair — covered in dust, carrying a flaming pipe — and the leaf catches fire.

entries.span: the length of one belly crawl
entries.detail: The actor erupts into flame; Darian goes for the smashed-glass alarm on his belly through the heat, debris under his hands, a flame whip missing by inches. He pulls the handle.

Water everywhere; the fire hisses down; Darian inventories his hands — soot, scratches, small burns, alive. Then the room turns cold: frost, icicles, an ice body with glowing eyes, and a fist frozen stuck in the surface.
The lord of the Dark Shores out-reasons an entire television studio: everything stops. Ice mid-advance, weapons half-lowered, and whatever runs the show FLINCHES.
Velvet from the whole ceiling; crew voices; cut the feed. When the curtains open the studio has reset itself to the break room — no flames, no ice, one television showing static.

Wario walks in clapping and applause comes out of the dark — Oscar-worthy, he says, brilliant special effects — until a lord who checks the building's work looks at the seats and finds every one of them EMPTY.

Evil Mario, still there, half in shadow, red eyes tracking the Director to the door — smiles slowly, and points one finger at the door the Director left through.

entries.beat: The correction, received in the field
entries.detail: The full account of the promo morning catches the archivist mid-emergency and the teaser is amended on the spot, in pencil, in the field posture: PORTAL FAILED, Luigi missing, a Mario-shaped thing out of a television. The word teaser enters the archive's vocabulary that evening, in a building with no honest clock, and it is not leaving.

entries.span: ten bought minutes, and two paragraphs read under duress
entries.detail: Four Iron Legion operatives introduce themselves by colour and take Toad Lee and Waluigi as leverage against one overdue Aegis Magi contract — cuffs, not cages, and the archivist is out of his before anybody notices and keeps wearing them anyway. Hjumpik buys ten minutes and reads [[prop:prop_accords_900_20_containment|six pages of the Autumnwood Accords]] standing up. The question that keeps the pocket book busy all night opens here: who sends a Colour Division across a planar boundary to collect one dwarf?

The thing wearing Lady Aurelian states its whole plan — collapse the manor, grow trees in the ruin, the beauty of nature is slow — and answers to the name Carnivorous. Red's poisoned dinner goes into its chest, the glamour comes apart, and the floor opens. Witnessed, not reconstructed: the archivist was in this building. Filed in full in the doorway filing.

entries.span: the rest of the night; no lamp was involved
entries.detail: In custody, cuffed by choice, the archivist works the question. The archive already holds the answer's shape: the arrangement — payments between the Iron Legion and Regency officials with the Chancellor's own signature on them — and the Mages' Guild's privileged access to Regency facilities, the same Guild whose failed contract the colours just collected like a household errand. Three names, one machine. The pocket book's next question writes itself: where does a machine like that keep its money?

entries.time: Night — the archive's maps, from memory
entries.detail: The maps say Yale Shores is an actual place, and an archivist who cannot recall his own maps in a building with no lamp deserves what the building does to him: Port Yale, the largest port on the western coast — seven thousand souls, a melting pot and a den of pirates and smugglers — under Fort Yale's guns; the Crimson Fleet's Smuggler's Cove running goods past the Regency's own tariffs; a graveyard reef that has claimed hundreds of hulls; a lighthouse nobody relit; pearl-divers, a crab kingdom with a foreign policy, star-fall on a ley-line beach; and one sea serpent, sole occupant of a trench the maps rate stronger than the fort. Rich, Guild-aligned, not militarized, no Legion garrison — the province where the money enters the kingdom, guarded by nobody because everyone is already paid. The Mages' Guild's own Astral Spire stands over all of it.

entries.time: Night — the dossier, read again from memory
entries.span: one file the archive has never once been able to close
entries.detail: The head of the Regency is Chancellor Toadsworth, the son who inherited everything — his father's journals allegedly confess to enabling Peach's assassination, and the inheritance is filed verbatim: 'My son inherits what I built. He inherits the secrets with it.' Villain, or victim of the wrong father: the archive holds both readings and cannot close the file. What it CAN file: the arrangement carries his own signature, and the archive can now add that he sits under Loyalist house arrest while the machine's paperwork stayed current without him. The leader's true nature, as far as this archive will file it: not the engine — the HEIR. The next day proved the trade sails from his own coast whether he signs it or not. WAH.
